findings.title: validate_interop is the G9 gate but cannot detect the corruption it gates: ElementTree does not enforce xml:id uniqueness and the OntoLex check is a substring count
findings.invariant: A gate with blocks_print=true must fail when the artifact it validates is structurally invalid. TEI/XML requires xml:id values to be unique within a document; an OntoLex Turtle release must be a well-formed graph, not merely a file containing a substring.
findings.failure_scenario: Run `python src/validate_interop.py --dir release` against the committed release/. It prints `interop validation OK: TEI entries=120173 | OntoLex entries=120173 | reverse rows=209319` and exits 0 — while that same release/tei_lex0.xml carries 12,374 distinct xml:id values that each occur more than once (e.g. `xml:id="pwg-A"` at lines 24686, 84705, 213094, all with `<orth>A</orth>`). `xml.etree.ElementTree.parse` is a non-validating well-formedness parser and has no xml:id awareness, so duplicates pass. validate_ontolex never parses Turtle at all — `text.count('ontolex:LexicalEntry')` would pass on a file consisting solely of that literal string. Consequence: roadmap/quality_gates.jsonl:9 records G9_schema_ci_interop as `"status":"passing","blocks_print":true` with the evidence line "release/tei_lex0.xml validates with 120173 entries", so every downstream go/no-go that reads gate status treats a document 12,374 duplicate-ID-corrupt as clean.
findings.evidence: validate_interop.py:24-30 — `root = ET.parse(path).getroot()` … `entries = root.findall('.//{http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0}entry')` … `return len(entries)` (no id collection, no uniqueness assert). validate_interop.py:39-42 — `n = text.count('ontolex:LexicalEntry')` / `if n < 1: fail(...)`. Measured: `grep -o 'xml:id="[^"]*"' release/tei_lex0.xml | sort | uniq -d | wc -l` → 12374.
findings.existing_test_gap: Nothing under tests/ references export_interop or validate_interop (grep over tests/ returns no file). The only coverage is .github/workflows/ci.yml:399-400, which runs the exporter over `src/fixtures/assembled_card.fixture.jsonl` — a ONE-entry fixture, in which a duplicate xml:id is arithmetically impossible. The gate is therefore exercised only on input that cannot exhibit the defect.
findings.fix_boundary: validate_interop.py: collect `{http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace}id` from every element during validate_tei and fail on a repeat; parse ontolex.ttl with rdflib (already a dependency — lod_acceptance.py:40) instead of counting a substring. quality_gates.jsonl G9 status must be recomputed after the check is real.

corrections:
Three corrections, all to blast radius and framing, none to the mechanism.

(1) The "12,374 duplicate-ID-corrupt" characterization overstates semantic harm. I hashed every entry body: 12,373 of the 12,374 duplicate-id groups are BYTE-IDENTICAL copies. These are the redundant sibling entries that HOMOGRAPH_KEYING_FIX_2026-06-30.md explicitly parks as "separate, pre-existing ... out of scope here ... an edition-modelling choice for the renderer stage". Combined with zero IDREF-style `#` pointers anywhere in tei_lex0.xml, nothing resolves these ids and no consumer is served wrong data by them. The finding's chosen example, `pwg-A` at lines 24686/84705/213094, is one of the harmless ones — all three bodies hash identically. Against those 12,373 a maintainer CAN say "yes, and that is fine for now"; only the formal XML/TEI-Lex-0 invalidity remains.

(2) The finding missed the one collision that is genuinely corrupting, and it is worse than what was reported. `pwg-U` is the sole duplicate-id group whose bodies differ, because `safe_id()` (export_interop.py:36-37) maps the distinct headwords `U` and `U~` onto the same identifier. This one is NOT fixed by the 2026-06-30 `idn` counter — that counter keys on key1, and `U` / `U~` are different key1 values, so both get idn==1. I re-simulated the current exporter over the real 120,173 headwords: regenerating the release today STILL emits a duplicate `pwg-U`. The defect is permanent in current code, not merely stale-artifact residue.

(3) The OntoLex half is not hypothetical, as the finding presents it ("would pass on a file consisting solely of that literal string"). The same collision lands in the committed release/ontolex.ttl as real graph corruption: line 74402 `pwg:U a ontolex:LexicalEntry ; ontolex:canonicalForm [ ontolex:writtenRep "U"@sa-Latn ]` and line 74419 `pwg:U a ontolex:LexicalEntry ; ontolex:canonicalForm [ ontolex:writtenRep "U~"@sa-Latn ]` — one IRI, two distinct Sanskrit lexical entries, which any RDF consumer merges into a single node carrying both canonicalForms. A substring count cannot see it; rdflib would. Relatedly the gate's own reported number is wrong: `text.count('ontolex:LexicalEntry')` = 120,173 but distinct entry subjects = 106,082, so the quality_gates.jsonl G9 evidence line "release/ontolex.ttl contains 120173 lexical entries" overstates the actual graph by ~13%.

Severity: P1, not P0. The gate is genuinely blind, is blocks_print=true, runs on the live release path, and propagates unchecked into the edition cut — but the realized data corruption is one entry pair out of 120,173 plus formal invalidity, not 12,374 corrupt entries. The fix_boundary stands and should be widened: uniqueness must be enforced on the EMITTED id/IRI (post-safe_id), not on key1, or `U`/`U~` collide again on the next regeneration.

Two details are wrong and should be restated. (1) Mechanism: the 12,374 duplicates are NOT what today's exporter produces. `export_interop.py:134-136` already de-duplicates same-key1 homographs (the 2026-06-30 fix), and regenerating from the live data yields exactly ONE duplicate id — `pwg-U`, from a `safe_id` collision between key1 `U` and `U~` where the `idn` counter is keyed on the raw key1 rather than on the emitted id. The correct statement is: the committed `release/` is stale/corrupt relative to its own generator, and validate_interop is structurally incapable of noticing — which is the more damning framing, since the exporter fix explicitly cited "the prior invalid-TEI duplicate-ID collision". The residual generator bug (safe_id collision) is 1 in 120,172, not 12,374. (2) fix_boundary is partly wrong: "parse ontolex.ttl with rdflib" would NOT catch the OntoLex corruption — I parsed the committed 32 MB file successfully (649,746 triples). Colliding subjects are legal RDF; the 12,374 collisions silently merge 14,091 entries into other headwords' subjects (120,173 declarations → 106,082 distinct entries). The real check is a distinct-subject count equal to the declaration count (and a distinct-xml:id count equal to the entry count), plus a staleness check that the committed release matches a fresh export.

findings.title: Both shipped interop artifacts are stale and corrupt: 12,374 duplicated xml:id in tei_lex0.xml and the same 12,374 merged subjects in ontolex.ttl, while the G9 gate reports both as validating
findings.invariant: xml:id must be unique within an XML document (XML ID validity). A gate marked blocks_print=true must fail on a structurally invalid artifact.
findings.failure_scenario: release/tei_lex0.xml contains 120,173 xml:id attributes but only 106,082 distinct values: 12,374 ids repeat, 14,091 occurrences are duplicates (pwg-ac x6, pwg-idam x5, pwg-as x5, pwg-a x3, pwg-aMSa x4 ...). Any consumer resolving by id -- XPath id(), getElementById, an RDF/TEI ingest keyed on xml:id -- silently binds to whichever entry it meets first. `python src/validate_interop.py --dir release` nevertheless prints 'interop validation OK: TEI entries=120173' and exits 0, and roadmap/quality_gates.jsonl records G9_schema_ci_interop as passing with blocks_print=true.
findings.affected: the published TEI-Lex0 artifact and every downstream consumer of it; 14,091 entry references
findings.evidence: Measured on the frozen commit: `grep -o 'xml:id="[^"]*"' release/tei_lex0.xml | wc -l` = 120173; `| sort -u | wc -l` = 106082; `| sort | uniq -d | wc -l` = 12374. Parsed with a regex over <entry xml:id=..><form><orth>..: 12,373 of the 12,374 duplicated ids have IDENTICAL <orth>, i.e. the same key1 emitted more than once; exactly ONE (pwg-U, for orth 'U' and 'U~') is a genuine safe_id() collapse of two distinct key1 values. Executed reproducer repro_teiid.py: a 3-row fixture with one repeated key1 run through the CURRENT src/export_interop.py emits pwg-agni, pwg-agni-2, pwg-agni-3 -- UNIQUE. The shipped artifact therefore was not produced by the exporter now in the tree: export_interop.py:133-135 carries `idn[key1] += 1` with the comment 'unique xml:id across same-key1 homograph entries'. The artifact's teiHeader matches export_interop.export_tei byte-for-byte in wording, so it is that exporter at an earlier state.
findings.existing_test_gap: Nothing under tests/ references export_interop or validate_interop. CI exercises the exporter only over src/fixtures/assembled_card.fixture.jsonl -- a ONE-entry fixture, in which a duplicate id is unrepresentable. validate_interop.validate_tei counts entries and never collects ids; validate_ontolex never parses Turtle at all (`text.count('ontolex:LexicalEntry')`).
findings.fix_boundary: Two separable acts: (1) re-cut release/tei_lex0.xml (and re-check the sibling ontolex.ttl and reverse_index.jsonl) from the current exporter, and (2) make validate_interop assert xml:id uniqueness and parse the Turtle with rdflib, which the repo already depends on and already uses in lod_acceptance.py. Do NOT do (1) without (2), or the next drift is equally invisible.

corrections: Two corrections, neither weakening the finding. (1) The sibling ontolex.ttl is not merely "to be re-checked" — it carries the IDENTICAL defect from the same stale generation: 120,173 `pwg:X a ontolex:LexicalEntry` subjects, 106,082 distinct, 12,374 repeated, and ZERO `_N`-suffixed subjects (the current exporter's ontolex path applies the same idn counter at export_interop.py:158-162). In RDF a repeated subject is not a parse error, so it fails even more silently: 14,091 homograph entries' senses are merged onto another entry's IRI. Any fix must re-cut both files, and the ontolex half will never be caught by an XML-ID check. (2) Line reference: `idn[key1] += 1` is at export_interop.py:134, not 133-135 (the surrounding block spans 132-137). (3) Severity: P1 rather than P0 — the corruption is confined to a derived interop artifact with no in-repo consumer that resolves by id, and G9's evidence string accurately reports what validate_interop printed, so the gate is weak rather than mendacious.

One wording correction, which also changes the fix. The title's "the current src/export_interop.py would emit unique ones" is not strictly true: measured on the real full card set the current exporter still emits ONE duplicate, pwg-U. The cause is a live bug the finding treats as benign: the uniquifier counts the RAW key1 (`idn[key1]`, :134 and :158) while the identifier is built from `safe_id(key1)` (:135, :159). Two distinct key1 values that normalize to the same safe_id (here "U" and "U~", since safe_id strips non-[A-Za-z0-9_] and then strips '_') each get idn == 1 and both render as pwg-U / pwg:U. So fix_boundary act (1) — re-cutting the release — does NOT by itself produce a uniquely-identified artifact; the counter must be keyed on safe_id(key1), not key1, in BOTH export_tei and export_ontolex, or the re-cut ships one guaranteed collision and validate_interop's new uniqueness assertion will fail the re-cut file. Also worth folding into the fix boundary: the corruption is not confined to tei_lex0.xml — release/ontolex.ttl carries the identical 12,374 collapses, and there it is a silent RDF subject MERGE (senses of different homographs unify onto one LexicalEntry), which is strictly worse than an ambiguous XPath id() bind. The finding lists ontolex.ttl only as something to "re-check"; it is measurably already broken.

findings.lead_adjudication: CONFIRMED by an independent verifier who re-measured both halves from scratch rather than trusting my counts, and who strengthened the finding twice. (1) The corruption is not confined to the TEI: release/ontolex.ttl carries 120,173 `pwg:X a ontolex:LexicalEntry` subjects, 106,082 distinct, the same 12,374 repeating — and in RDF that is worse than in XML, because duplicate subjects are perfectly legal and simply MERGE, so 14,091 entries' senses are silently unioned onto the wrong lexical entry inside a 649,746-triple published graph, with no error anywhere. I re-measured this myself and confirm the identical numbers. (2) The reproduction was done at full scale, not on my 3-row fixture: running the real `export_interop.py tei` over the real 120,172-card assembled_cards.jsonl yields exactly ONE duplicate id (pwg-U) instead of 12,374, so the shipped artifact demonstrably predates the exporter now in the tree. A third signal of the same staleness: the shipped TEI has 120,173 entries while its stated source assembled_cards.jsonl has 120,172 records — one more entry than the source it names, and no gate compares the two counts.

findings.title: `~~h<N>` in a subcard key is a 0-based index over homonym blocks, not a homonym number, so 1,278 of 5,211 mappable store rows carry a printed column that is not their own record's
findings.invariant: A card's `column`/`volume`/`page` must be the printed location of THAT card's entry. The docstring at pwg_page_index.py:145 states the contract explicitly: "primary (lowest-volume, homonym-matched) start column".
findings.failure_scenario: Store rows carry subcard keys of the form `deva~~h0_00_pwg00` (promote_final_cards.py:1207,1230) so `SUB_HOM_RE` (pwg_page_index.py:136) yields card_h='0'. PWG `<h>` values start at 1, so `card_h in src_homs` (line 166) is always False for the `~~h0_` majority and control falls to `sel = cand` (line 169) — every record sharing the key1. `starts[0]` (line 176) then picks the lowest (vol,col) across ALL homographs. Verified on csl-orig pwg.txt: key1 `agnihotra` owns records at (1,36,h=1), (1,37,h=2), (1,1147,h=None), (5,949,h=1), (5,949,h=2), (7,1687,h=None) — every agnihotra card gets column '1-0036'/page '1-p0018' regardless of which sense it translated. The real-homonym path is broken too: for `akArya` a card with card_h='1' DOES match src_homs={'1'}, but line 167 admits `e.h is None` records as well, so sel={(1,9,None),(1,199,'1'),(5,943,None)} and starts[0]=(1,9) → column '1-0009', page '1-p0005', while homonym 1 actually starts at column 199 (page 100).
findings.affected: Every promoted card whose key1 owns more than one PWG record — 13,900 headwords / 17,284 surplus source records; plus the 46 groups where an explicit homonym match is still overridden by an <h>-less sibling.
findings.existing_test_gap: pwg_page_index.py has no --selftest and no file under RussianTranslation/tests/ names it; the only verification is the `matched/total` line printed at pwg_page_index.py:220. That counter increments at line 183 for every homograph-pooled guess, so the operator-facing statistic reports 100% success precisely in the failing case — the wrong denominator hides the defect.
findings.fix_boundary: pwg_page_index.py annotate_cards (lines 158-183): the homonym-selection branch and what `column`/`volume`/`page` are allowed to assert when selection is ambiguous. `pc_all`/`page_all` are already honest; the scalar fields should be omitted (or flagged ambiguous) rather than picked when len(starts) > 1 and no exact homonym match exists.

corrections:
Two corrections, both of which make the finding stronger or narrower rather than wrong.
(1) Root cause is deeper than "PWG <h> starts at 1". `~~hN_` is not a homonym number at all: it is a 0-based `enumerate` index over homonym blocks, built at RussianTranslation/src/_pilot_gen_merged.py:524 (`for hom, (dl, cards, npfx) in enumerate(segmented)` -> `sub = '%s~~h%d_00_%s' % (root, hom, label)` at :529/:562). Measured against the cards' own `<hom>N.</hom>` markers, `~~h0_` maps to `<hom>1` (113x), `<hom>2` (48x), `<hom>3` (33x), `<hom>4` (17x), `<hom>5` (15x), … and never to `<hom>0`. So line 166 is not merely dead for the `~~h0_` majority (9,670/11,603 rows) — for the 498 `~~h1_` rows it MATCHES and matches the wrong homonym, systematically off by one. The join key is semantically invalid on both branches, which the finding's prose does not say.
(2) The akArya illustration is source-side only — there is no akArya card in the live store (I grepped store_copy.jsonl; zero rows). The claim is fine as a source-data demonstration but should be swapped for a live one: `As` / `Bid` / `Buj` all show the "explicit homonym match overridden" shape on real store rows (e.g. `_bid~~h0_zz_pw01`, card text `<hom>2.</hom>`, stamped 5-0281, which is the start column of Bid homonym 1).
(3) Scope framing: "13,900 headwords affected" is a source-side count of ambiguous key1 values. The store-side number is 10,733 of the 11,251 annotated rows sitting on an ambiguous key1; of the 477 rows where an independent ground truth exists, 24.8%-43% are demonstrably wrong. The public co-location panel (pilot/build_article_site.py:705) is NOT affected — it reads pwg_columns.tsv keyed by headword, not the store scalar — so the blast radius is the store plus the TTL/TEI and MDF exports, not the site.

Two corrections. (1) BLAST RADIUS is wrong by ~300x and must be restated against the live store, not pwg.txt: "13,900 headwords / 17,284 surplus records" is source-side potential. The store holds only 254 distinct key1; 46 have len(pc_all) > 1; and 1,278 of 5,211 mappable pwg-layer rows (24.5%), across 45 headwords, carry a `column` that is not their own record's printed column. (2) ROOT CAUSE is misidentified. The finding blames `card_h='0'` never matching `src_homs`. The real defect is a type confusion: `~~h<N>` is a 0-based INDEX into the record list for that headword (_pilot_gen_merged.py:524 `enumerate(segmented)`, with `htag = ' homonym %d' % (hom + 1)` confirming hom+1 is the human homonym), while `e.h` is PWG's 1-based printed `<h>`. Consequently the branch the finding treats as the working one is the more dangerous: card_h='1' DOES match src_homs and silently stamps homonym 1's column on homonym 2's card. Canonical live example, better than the finding's akArya: `han~~h1_00_pwg00` (its own `h` field reads "han [омоним 2]") is stamped `column 7-1494` / `page 7-p0747`, whereas PWG homonym 2 (L115990) starts at `7-1512` / `7-p0756`. Worst live case: `_ap~~h2_*` (record printed at `5-1107`, page `5-p0554`) stamped `1-0649` / `1-p0325` — wrong volume. The fix boundary should therefore also cover the index-vs-<h> join, not only the ambiguity guard: omitting the scalars when `len(starts) > 1` still leaves the off-by-one wrong whenever the false match narrows sel to a single column (e.g. `vas~~h1`, pc_all `['6-0825']`).

findings.lead_adjudication: CONFIRMED by both lenses, and both corrected it in the same direction. Correctness settled that the field is load-bearing: export_de_edition.py:79 allowlists exactly volume/page/column (deliberately NOT pc_all/page_all) and :340-343 emits pwglex:page / pwglex:volume on a per-SENSE subject that also carries pwglex:homonym — so a wrong column ships into the published DE edition graph beside a homonym label that contradicts it. Two corrections adopted. (1) Blast radius, restated against the live store instead of pwg.txt: not '13,900 headwords / 17,284 surplus records' (that is source-side potential) but 1,278 of 5,211 mappable pwg-layer rows — 24.5%, across 45 headwords — carrying a column that is not their own record's printed column. (2) Root cause is a type confusion, not an off-by-one: `~~h<N>` is a 0-based enumerate index over homonym blocks (_pilot_gen_merged.py:524-529), and measured against the cards' own <hom>N.</hom> markers `~~h0_` maps to <hom>1 113x, <hom>2 48x, <hom>3 33x, <hom>4 17x, <hom>5 15x and never to <hom>0. The finding's 'PWG <h> starts at 1' explanation is therefore wrong even though its conclusion is right.

findings.title: `ord` is a positional index into a live upstream file but is persisted as a stable record identity
findings.invariant: The store's record identity must survive an upstream insert. run_batch.py:434 states the invariant it relies on: "ord:… ids are stable".
findings.failure_scenario: `ord` is `enumerate(pwg_mask.records())` — the ordinal position of a record inside csl-orig/v02/pwg/pwg.txt. `done_ids()` reads those ordinals back out of the store and `cmd_build` skips them. Cologne inserts supplement/Nachtrag records into pwg.txt (both pwg_mask.py:39 and pwg_page_index.py:41 document the resulting float L-ids, e.g. `26305.290`, as "Cologne supplement/Nachtrag records, 635 records"). One insert at position k shifts every ord >= k by +1. On the next `cmd_build`, the ordinal of an already-done record now names its NEIGHBOUR: that neighbour is skipped as done and is never translated, never queued, and never reported — the only counter is the aggregate `skipped` at line 185, which folds it in with round-trip and length rejects. Simultaneously every persisted review id `ord:NNNN` (line 111) re-points to a different headword. The module already has drift machinery for `row:NNNNNN:` ids (`_REVIEW_POS_PREFIX`, line 429, and the comment at line 440 "Positional 'row:NNNNNN:' ids drift") but explicitly exempts `ord:` on a premise that does not hold.
findings.affected: Every record positioned after any future upstream insert — silently skipped from translation with no per-record diagnostic; plus every persisted `ord:` review id.
findings.evidence:
run_batch.py:159-161 —
        for ordi, buf in enumerate(pwg_mask.records()):
            if ordi in done:
                continue
run_batch.py:86-95 —
    def done_ids():
        ids = set()
        ... ids.add(json.loads(line)['ord'])
run_batch.py:433-434 —
    """Position-independent tail of a positional review id ('subcard:<sub>#<tag>').
    Returns '' when the id carries no positional prefix (ord:… ids are stable)."""
The store already carries `key1` beside `ord` (line 233), so the mismatch is detectable — but nothing anywhere reconciles ord against key1.
findings.existing_test_gap: No test replays `cmd_build` against a pwg.txt with a record inserted before an already-done ordinal. The selftests that touch pwg_mask.records() (pwg_mask.py:435, window_selftest.py:2544) all verify mask/restore round-trip on a single body, which is orthogonal to positional identity.
findings.fix_boundary: run_batch.py done_ids()/cmd_build (lines 86-95, 159-161) and `_display_ord`/`review_id` (lines 109-125): the skip set must key on a content-derived identity (key1 + <h> + L-id, or the existing provenance.input_raw_sha256) rather than on enumeration position, and `ord:` ids must be treated as positional like `row:` ids already are.

corrections: The finding inverts what is actually true of `ord`. It is not "a positional index persisted as a stable identity" — it is persisted nowhere in live data at all. The genuine (and much narrower) observation available here is the opposite one: `done_ids()` is already permanently inert, because the merged/promoted pipeline that produced all 11,603 live rows stopped writing `ord`, so `run_batch.py build`'s advertised resume ("Resumable: `build` skips records already in the store", docstring line 7) would today re-emit from ordinal 0 and re-queue already-translated records. That is a stale-docstring/dead-lane hygiene issue on a retired code path, not a silent-data-loss P1, and it is already recorded in review/G5_REJECT_REQUEUE_AUDIT.md. The severity is inflated by three steps: the affected-set is not "every record after any future upstream insert" but zero records; the "persisted `ord:` review ids" number zero, not "every" one; and the claimed upstream insertion stream has produced no record-count change in any of the 37 available pwg.txt commits.

Three corrections. (a) "every persisted review id `ord:NNNN` (line 111) re-points to a different headword" — no such persisted id exists: 0 of 11,603 store rows and 0 of 11,163 review-queue rows produce an `ord:` id; all 11,603 are `row:` ids, which the module already de-drifts by subcard tail. (b) The affected-scope claim "Every record positioned after any future upstream insert — silently skipped" is wrong even in the hypothetical: after a +1 shift only records whose new ordinal happens to sit in `done` are skipped (bounded by |done|), while the records at the old ordinals get re-emitted as duplicates — it is a shifted-set collision, not "everything after the insert". (c) The premise the docstring at :433-434 is accused of getting wrong ("ord:… ids are stable") is currently vacuously true rather than false: the `ord`-writing producer (`cmd_collect`, the only STORE appender) has not written the live store, the pipeline moved to subcard rows, and the upstream file's record count has never changed in any available commit. The real residual is a latent trap conditional on reviving the legacy build/collect path — worth a one-line note or a key1-vs-ord assertion, not a P1.

findings.title: Weekly cost ceiling silently ignores every dollar spent by a window that times out
findings.invariant: R3.2: "the week is the only wall" — every USD the lane spends must be counted against weekly_cost_ceiling before the next tick is allowed to dispatch.
findings.failure_scenario: An hourly tick dispatches bounded_staged_run; the child hangs (the §270 quota-hang class this module exists to detect) and `subprocess.run(..., timeout=4h)` raises TimeoutExpired at line 211. Control jumps straight to the handler at line 327, so the ledger-reading cost loop at lines 213-221 never runs and `record` gets no `window_cost_usd` key. `week_spend` (line 143) only sums records that HAVE that key, so the — real, already-billed — calls recorded in `<checkpoint>.calls.json` are invisible. Next tick reads spent=0, remaining=full ceiling, and dispatches again. A lane whose windows reliably time out can spend N × ceiling per week while the ledger reports $0.
findings.evidence: nonstop_scheduler.py:211 `proc = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, encoding='utf-8', timeout=cfg.get('window_timeout', 4 * 3600))` — the cost accumulation at :214-221 (`ledger = json.load(open(checkpoint + '.calls.json'...)); ... cost += float(usage['observed_cost_usd'])`) is unreachable on timeout. tick :317 `record['window_cost_usd'] = cost` is likewise unreachable; the handler at :327-330 `except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as exc: return done('window_failed', 'runner_timeout', failed_step=_step_of(exc), timeout_s=...)` records no cost. week_spend :143 `if rec.get('week') == week and rec.get('window_cost_usd'):`.
findings.existing_test_gap: The module's own selftest case (8b) at nonstop_scheduler.py:488-497 raises TimeoutExpired from bounded_run and asserts only `verdict`, `reason`, `failed_step`, `timeout_s` — it never asserts that the spend was recovered.
