findings.fix_boundary: nonstop_scheduler.py Runners.bounded_run — wrap the subprocess.run in try/finally (or catch TimeoutExpired locally) so the `<checkpoint>.calls.json` cost is read and returned on every exit path, and have tick() stamp `window_cost_usd` before re-raising to the timeout handler.

corrections: The defect is NOT timeout-conditional and the proposed fix is a no-op. nonstop_scheduler.py:216 reads `ledger.get('calls')` from a `pwg.call_reservation.v1` file whose only container is `runs[<run_id>]['reservations']`, so `bounded_run` returns cost=0.0 and rows=[] on EVERY path, including a clean exit-0 window (proven against three real ledgers holding $4.30, $2.15 and $1.32). week_spend additionally drops a recorded 0.0 because of its truthiness guard, so `spent` is 0 every tick regardless of timeouts. The correct fix boundary is line 216 (sum `observed_cost_usd` over `runs[*].reservations[*].telemetry`, or better, read the ledger's own cumulative `runs[*].usage`), not a try/finally around subprocess.run. Same line also makes `classify_quota_hang(rows)`永 unreachable-by-data, so the §270 pause never fires either. Blast radius should be scoped down: the lane is registered DISABLED and has never dispatched a live window (no scheduler_ticks_*.jsonl exists), so no dollars are presently at risk — this is a latent go-live blocker, not active leakage, hence P2 not P1.

The defect is real but the mechanism is narrower in the write-up than in the code, and the true scope is WIDER. `bounded_run` reads `ledger.get('calls') or []`, while the real `pwg.call_reservation.v1` file is `{'schema': ..., 'runs': {run_id: {'reservations': [...]}}}` — verified against two production `.calls.json` files on disk. So `rows` is ALWAYS `[]` and `cost` is ALWAYS `0.0`, on the clean path as much as on the timeout path: my control run (arm B, child exits 0) produced `"window_cost_usd": 0.0` against a ledger holding $3.00. Consequences: (a) `week_spend` is structurally always $0 and the R3.2 weekly wall NEVER binds, timeout or not — the timeout arm is one instance of a total accounting failure, not the cause; (b) a second casualty on the same lines — `classify_quota_hang(rows)` at :323 always receives `[]`, so the §270 quota-hang pause-until-reset (the module's other safety valve) can never fire either. The fix boundary must therefore include correcting the ledger key/traversal (`data['runs'][*]['reservations']`, or reuse `call_reservation` itself), not only moving the read into a try/finally. Severity stays P1 rather than P0 only because the Task Scheduler job is currently Disabled and the lane has never ticked; on enable the defect is active from tick 1 at $50/window, hourly.

findings.title: provenance.pipeline.prompt_version stamped on every promoted row does not cover the prompt that produced the row
findings.invariant: pipeline_version.py:8 declares the contract: 'prompt — pwg_ru_prompts/ (translate / judge / corpus-check prompts)', and pipeline_version.py:141-144 `check()` is the 'forgotten-bump guard' that fires when the prompt files changed but the version was not bumped. Every promoted row carries this stamp so that a later prompt bugfix can identify which rows must be re-translated (promote_final_cards.py:391-393). For that to be true, the hashed file set must be the bytes actually sent to the model.
findings.failure_scenario: The current headless PWG lane builds its prompt as `preamble + translation + grammar + [nws] + card blocks` (headless_worker.py:532-534). `preamble` is the Python constant MASK_PREAMBLE (gen_opt_harness2.py:715, wired in at :1559 as `'preamble': MASK_PREAMBLE.replace(...)`), and `translation` is the TR block scraped out of src/pilot/run_pilot_wf.js (gen_opt_harness2.py:699-706). Neither file matches `pwg_ru_prompts/*.txt` or `pwg_ru_prompts/*.md`, and neither is in the `script` component's file list either. So: edit MASK_PREAMBLE to change the masking regime, run a window, promote. Every new row is stamped `prompt_version: '1.1.0'` with an UNCHANGED `prompt_sha` ('9983b21651493256'), `python pipeline_version.py check` reports no drift, and `find_stale` (pipeline_version.py:203-215) will never select those rows for re-run. Rows produced by two materially different prompts are indistinguishable in the store — which is exactly the claim this field exists to make (see the H1957 note the module itself writes at :120-127 about a memoized sha producing 'a row claiming to have been produced by code it was not produced by').
findings.affected: The `provenance.pipeline` stamp on every row promoted by promote_final_cards.py and promote_en.py (promote_en.py:172), and every downstream re-run-targeting decision made by pipeline_version.find_stale / audit_translation_provenance.py.
findings.evidence: pipeline_versions.json:10-13 `"files": [ "pwg_ru_prompts/*.txt", "pwg_ru_prompts/*.md" ]` for `prompt`; :33-40 the `script` list is only run_batch.py / pwg_mask.py / corpus_gate.py / assemble.py / promote_final_cards.py / annotate_stats.py — gen_opt_harness2.py and headless_worker.py appear in neither. gen_opt_harness2.py:715 `MASK_PREAMBLE = """=== MASKED + BATCHED REGIME (read first — overrides input-format details below) ===`; :1559 `'preamble': MASK_PREAMBLE.replace('`russian`', '`%s`' % field),`. gen_opt_harness2.py:700 `src = read_text(os.path.join(REPO, 'src', 'pilot', 'run_pilot_wf.js'))` / :701 `m = re.search(r'const TR = `(.*?)`\n', src, re.S)`. headless_worker.py:532 `stable = prompt['preamble'] + prompt['translation']`. pipeline_version.py:131-135 `for name in COMPONENTS: comp = manifest['components'][name]; out['%s_version' % name] = comp['version']; out['%s_sha' % name] = component_sha(comp['files'], root)`. promote_final_cards.py:393 `'pipeline': pipeline_version.stamp(model_version=model_version),`. Supporting: `git log --oneline -- RussianTranslation/src/pilot/gen_opt_harness2.py` shows two commits after the last touch of pipeline_versions.json.
findings.existing_test_gap: pipeline_version.py's own selftest (:399-428) builds a throwaway tree containing only `pwg_ru_prompts/1.txt` and a manifest whose files are `['pwg_ru_prompts/*.txt']` — it verifies the hashing mechanism against a fixture it invented, never against the real manifest or the real prompt builders. No test in tests/ imports pipeline_version, and none asserts that the union of the component globs covers every file that contributes bytes to a dispatched prompt.
findings.fix_boundary: pipeline_versions.json `components.prompt.files` (and `components.script.files`) — add `src/pilot/gen_opt_harness2.py` (or extract MASK_PREAMBLE into a pwg_ru_prompts/ text file) and `src/pilot/run_pilot_wf.js`, then re-freeze. Add a coverage assertion next to pipeline_version.check() that the manifest's globs include every path the live prompt builders read.

corrections: Three detail corrections, none load-bearing. (a) The failure_scenario claims "`python pipeline_version.py check` reports no drift". False at the frozen commit — check() already reports drift on all three components (prompt 9983b21651493256 -> 31656e0197b6c806, glossary ca1c632639627174 -> bb4626344404b1c1, script 144e83f802c72828 -> ebb543599bcdc005), because the recorded freeze is stale for unrelated reasons. The correct and stronger statement is that check()'s output is byte-identical before and after the MASK_PREAMBLE edit — it is blind to the edit, not silent overall. (b) The scenario says new rows are stamped with "an UNCHANGED prompt_sha ('9983b21651493256')". 9983b2... is the manifest's RECORDED sha; stamp() writes the CURRENT sha (31656e0197b6c806 here), and no live store row carries 9983b2... at all (the 811 sha-bearing rows carry five other values). The invariant that survives is "unchanged relative to itself across the edit". (c) The finding implies the corruption is live; it is not yet realized — MASK_PREAMBLE is byte-identical across all four commits of gen_opt_harness2.py in the repo history, so this is a latent contract hole. Two additions the finding misses and that strengthen it: stale_reasons (pipeline_version.py:175-191) never reads any *_sha, so re-run targeting rests entirely on a human bumping prompt.version, and check() is the only signal that could prompt that bump; and 10,792 of 11,603 live rows carry pipeline.backfilled:true with no prompt_sha/glossary_sha/script_sha at all, so for 93% of the store the sha layer is absent even in principle.

Three statements in the write-up are false as written and must be fixed before publication. (a) "`python pipeline_version.py check` reports no drift" — false at the frozen commit; check() already reports DRIFT on all three components because the recorded freeze is stale for unrelated reasons. The defensible claim is that check()'s output is *byte-identical before and after* a MASK_PREAMBLE edit — it is blind to that edit, not silent overall. (b) "stamped ... with an UNCHANGED prompt_sha ('9983b21651493256')" — false; 9983b2... is the manifest's RECORDED sha, while stamp() computes the CURRENT sha (31656e0197b6c806 today), and no live store row carries 9983b2... at all. (c) "find_stale will never select those rows for re-run" implies the glob affects re-run targeting; it does not — stale_reasons reads only `<name>_version`, never any sha, so re-run targeting depends solely on a human bumping prompt.version and is unchanged by this gap. Two facts should be added because they set the true severity: the failure is latent (MASK_PREAMBLE is byte-identical across all available commits, so no two live rows were in fact produced by different prompts under one stamp), and 10,792/11,603 rows are `backfilled` with no shas at all. Conversely, one point should be strengthened: the repo documents `pwg_ru_prompts/` as a design kit that never ran (`pwg_ru_prompts/README.md`, `1_perevod.txt`:4, PIPELINE_ARCHITECTURE.md:340/:358), so the `prompt` component is not merely incomplete — it hashes an artifact with zero causal relation to any promoted row, and its sha has in fact varied five times across the store for reasons that never touched the output. Reclassify P1 → P3: manifest/provenance hygiene, latent, no consumer dependency, guard already inert.

findings.title: promote_en reads the whole store outside the PromoteClaim and writes that snapshot back inside it — a concurrent promote is silently overwritten, recoverable only from the backup
findings.invariant: promote_lock.PromoteClaim must be held across the ENTIRE read-guard-write window of the canonical store (promote_lock.py:5-10: "nothing serializes the read-existing-store / merge-in-new-rows / os.replace window"); a full-store rewrite must be computed from a snapshot taken under the claim.
findings.failure_scenario: Lane A runs `promote_en.py --store <canonical>`; at line 504 it snapshots all N store rows into `rows`. Lane B (or a coordinator batch_promote) acquires the claim and commits 40 new RU sense rows, then releases. Lane A then acquires the claim at line 592, backs up (capturing B's version), and at line 607 writes back its N-row pre-B snapshot with EN attached. B's 40 rows are gone from the live store. Nothing in either run reports a conflict: A prints "wrote tri-lingual store -> ... (N rows ...)" and exits 0.
findings.affected: the whole canonical pwg_ru_translated.jsonl (every row promoted by a concurrent run), plus its EN attachment
findings.evidence: promote_en.py:504 `rows = [json.loads(l) for l in open(args.store, encoding='utf-8') if l.strip()]` — no claim held here. The claim is taken 88 lines later, promote_en.py:592 `with PromoteClaim(args.store, steal=args.steal_lock, **ttl_kwargs):`, and the write is promote_en.py:607 `_atomic_write_rows(args.store, rows)` — `rows` is the line-504 snapshot mutated in place by `attach()` (promote_en.py:560). The comment at promote_en.py:585-588 states the claim covers "the backup+write window", which is precisely the wrong window. Contrast the RU lane, which reads inside the claim: promote_final_cards.py:2079 `with claim_cm:` … :2092-2099 store read.
findings.existing_test_gap: promote_en.selftest (promote_en.py:305) is single-process and drives attach()/_atomic_write_rows on a fixture store; it asserts fsync-before-replace (promote_en.py:436-448) but never starts a second writer, so no test observes a store mutation between the read at 504 and the claim at 592. promote_lock.selftest (promote_lock.py:166) tests claim acquisition in isolation, not who reads what before acquiring.
findings.fix_boundary: Move the store read (promote_en.py:504) inside the `with PromoteClaim(...)` block at promote_en.py:592, or re-read + re-attach under the claim before `_atomic_write_rows`; the EN lane should also route through store_write.locked_store_rewrite, which owns lock+backup+atomic replace as one unit.

corrections: Two corrections. (1) The `fix_boundary` is wrong: "route through store_write.locked_store_rewrite, which owns lock+backup+atomic replace as one unit" would NOT fix this bug. `locked_store_rewrite(store, rows, ...)` at store_write.py:117-131 accepts an already-read `rows` list and only opens the claim at :131 — every one of its 17 callers reads the store outside the claim (annotate_dcs_freq.py:152 read / :193 write; annotate_evidence.py:367 read / :385 write). The same TOCTOU therefore exists in the module the codebase designates as "the ONE sanctioned rewrite path", so this is a class defect, not a promote_en outlier, and the real fix is either the first half of the stated boundary (move the read inside the `with PromoteClaim` at promote_en.py:592, as promote_final_cards.py:2092 does) or adding a read-inside/generation-check variant to store_write. (2) Blast radius is overstated as unrecoverable P0: the erased rows are preserved by the fsynced O_EXCL backup taken inside the claim at promote_en.py:597-598 (unique µs+pid+uuid name, `_en_backup_path`), so a rival's rows are recoverable from `<store>.preEN.*.bak` — the loss is silent, not permanent, except under `--no-backup`. Combined with 0/11,603 rows carrying `en` (promote_en has never run on the canonical store), this is P2 latent, rising to P1 only if the EN promote becomes a routine lane run alongside RU promotes or is run with `--no-backup`.

Three corrections. (1) The loss is RECOVERABLE, not unrecoverable: the `.preEN` backup at promote_en.py:595-598 is taken INSIDE the claim, i.e. AFTER the concurrent lane committed, so it captures the victim's rows — I verified the backup held 5 rows while the live store held 3. Total loss requires `--no-backup`. What is genuinely silent is DETECTION: both runs exit 0 and report success, so nobody knows to restore. (2) Reachability today is gated, so this is dormant-but-scheduled rather than actively losing rows: with default args promote_en.py exits at :502 (`no EN wf_output files matched`) because ROOT holds no `wf_output.en.*.json`; the live store carries 0 EN rows; and docs/ROADMAP_..._UNFREEZE_2026H2.md:46 and docs/IMPLEMENTATION_...:20 make "never run promote_en.py" a standing constraint for the current wave, with the real run scheduled for FU1 Phase 2. An operator must pass `--glob archive/legacy_runtime_2026-07-04/wf_output.en.*.json` to reach line 504 at all. (3) The fix_boundary is half wrong: routing through `store_write.locked_store_rewrite` does NOT fix this — store_write.py:117 also takes `rows` from the caller and never re-reads inside its own claim. Only moving the :504 read inside the `with PromoteClaim(...)` block (or re-read + re-attach under the claim before :607) closes it.

findings.lead_adjudication: CONFIRMED by both lenses; downgraded P0 -> P1 on their evidence, and both severity opinions were P1/P2. The invariant is required by live contract, not just by the reviewer: promote_lock.py's docstring says the claim exists to serialize 'the read-existing-store / merge-in-new-rows / os.replace window'; promote_final_cards.py:2073-2099 and batch_promote both read the store INSIDE the claim; and LANG_PARITY line 771 asserts as a SHARED verdict that the mechanism guards that window in 'promote_final_cards.py --merge AND promote_en.py' — which is false of the code. Three deflations adopted. (a) Latent, not realized: 0 of 11,603 live store rows carry `en`, so this path has never run against the canonical store. (b) Recoverable, not unrecoverable: the unique O_EXCL fsynced .preEN backup is taken INSIDE the claim, i.e. after the rival committed, so the rival's rows survive on disk — only --no-backup removes that net. (c) The window is narrow and the lane is a rare manual phase step. It survives because it is SILENT: neither run reports a conflict, and promote_en has no content-mass shrink guard, which promote_final_cards.py:695 does have.

findings.title: Two flags of the same promote entry point disagree on identical input: `--merge` refuses a 99.7% content-mass shed, `--ready-partial-report --apply` performs it silently
findings.invariant: Every path that replaces the canonical store must (a) read+merge under PromoteClaim, and (b) pass the same refusal gates as the single/batch lanes: duplicate sense identity, >50% row shrink, and refuse_content_mass_shrink.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator runs `promote_final_cards.py --ready-partial-report R.json --apply --store <canonical>`. The store is read at :222-226 and the merged row list is fixed at :231. A coordinator batch_promote commits between :231 and the claim at :236; the ready-partial run then writes its stale merge at :241, dropping the bundle. Separately, even with no concurrency, this path writes rows_to_write without ever evaluating `duplicates`, the 50%-shrink guard, or `refuse_content_mass_shrink` — so a store state that `main()` (:2154-2183) and `batch_promote` (:1032-1044) would both REFUSE is written here without a word.
findings.affected: canonical store rows from any promote that commits during the window; plus any store state the shared guards would have refused
findings.evidence: promote_final_cards.py:222 `existing_rows = []` … :226 `existing_rows.append(json.loads(line))`; :231 `rows_to_write, downgraded, protected = merge_store_rows(existing_rows, rows)`; only then :236 `claim_cm = PromoteClaim(store)` / :237 `with claim_cm:` / :241 `_atomic_write_rows(store, rows_to_write)`. No call to `refuse_content_mass_shrink` or the duplicate-identity `collections.Counter(identities)` check appears anywhere between :219 and :245, unlike main() (:2154 `refuse_content_mass_shrink(store_rows_before, rows_to_write, force=args.force)`) and batch_promote (:1044 same call, :1032-1037 duplicate check).
findings.existing_test_gap: The only callers are the in-file selftests (promote_final_cards.py:1803, 1814, 1817, 1826, 1835, 1946); all are single-threaded against a temp fixture store and none assert that the guards fire on this path. `grep -rn promote_ready_partial_clean` finds no file under tests/.
findings.fix_boundary: Hoist the `PromoteClaim(store)` to before the read at :222 (or re-read inside it) and route this path through the same guard sequence as main() — duplicate identity, shrink, refuse_content_mass_shrink — ideally by calling store_write.locked_store_rewrite.

corrections: Two details to tighten. (1) The finding's own existing_test_gap says "the only callers are the in-file selftests" — that is wrong and understates reachability: main() calls it at :1946 from the documented `--ready-partial-report` CLI flag, and because args.store defaults to DEFAULT_STORE the live canonical store is the target when --store is omitted, so the failure_scenario does not even need an explicit `--store <canonical>`. (2) The finding omits a mitigation: the write does take an fsynced timestamped `.premerge.*.bak` inside the claim (:238-240), and I verified it captures the racing writer's state, so the loss is silent but recoverable, not destructive-final. Also note this lane returns before validate_store_target (:2200), so the missing-store / --init-store contract check is skipped too — one more gate absent beyond the three named.

The defensible residue is narrow and is a hardening item, not a P1 correctness defect: `promote_ready_partial_clean` re-reads nothing after taking `PromoteClaim`, so a promote committing in the :231→:236 window is silently superseded (recoverable from the `.premerge.*.bak` the lane always takes inside the claim). That property is shared verbatim with `store_write.locked_store_rewrite` and its 17 mutator callers, so if it is worth fixing it should be fixed once in `store_write`, not singled out here. The gate-parity half should be dropped outright: duplicate-identity, 50%-shrink and `refuse_content_mass_shrink` are wf_output-rebuild guards on the two full-promote lanes, absent from the codebase's own sanctioned rewrite path, and the live store already violates the duplicate gate (4 duplicate identities), which means those gates would refuse rather than protect this lane. The one gap actually worth filing separately is that the `--ready-partial-report --apply` lane has no code fence against `args.store == DEFAULT_STORE` (only prose in the argparse help and the implementation doc) and returns at :1955 before `validate_store_target`, unlike the `--merge` lane's explicit DEFAULT_STORE refusal at :1968-1978. Also correct the finding's `existing_test_gap`: `main()` calls the function at :1946 from a documented CLI flag, so it is not selftest-only.

findings.lead_adjudication: The reproduction lens settles this by measurement, and the measurement is what the correctness lens does not dispose of. It built an 11-row fixture store and ran the two lanes on byte-identical copies: `--merge` exited 1 with 'REFUSED: would shed 99.7% of store content mass (6895 -> 20 chars) ... at row delta 11 -> 2', while the same inputs through `--ready-partial-report R.json --apply` exited 0, printed status 'applied', and rewrote the store 11 rows -> 2 with no warning and no --force. Both are dispatched from main() (:1941-1957, before validate_store_target and before every H2089 route guard), and `--store` defaults to DEFAULT_STORE, which resolves to the LIVE canonical store even from a worktree — so the scenario does not even require an explicit --store. The correctness lens makes a genuinely useful point that is adopted into the body: the three gates are rebuild-lane gates by their own comments, and the 17 mutators that write through store_write.locked_store_rewrite run none of them, so 'every store write must pass these gates' is not an invariant this codebase holds. But that argument explains the mutators; it does not explain why two flags of the same PROMOTE entry point, on identical input, disagree by 99.7% of content mass in silence. That asymmetry is the defect. Ruling: CONFIRMED at P1, retitled to the asymmetry. Not P0: an fsynced timestamped .premerge backup is taken inside the claim, and the destructive path requires an explicit --apply.

findings.title: lane_guard's automatic store revert rewrites the whole canonical store with NO PromoteClaim at all
findings.invariant: No writer may replace pwg_ru_translated.jsonl without holding promote_lock.PromoteClaim across its read-guard-write window (the whole point of H336/H-1 and of store_write.locked_store_rewrite, which exists so that non-promote mutators get the same guarantee).
findings.failure_scenario: `lane_spotcheck_tick.py --execute` fires on a lane that hit >=2 sev-3 defects; lane_guard.run -> revert_windows reads the store at :76-77 and writes `kept` at :96. A promote (or promote_en, or any locked_store_rewrite mutator) commits between those two lines: its rows are silently dropped, because revert_windows writes a full-file image derived from a snapshot it never guarded. In the mirror direction, a promote that reads before :96 and writes after it silently resurrects the reverted defective rows the freeze existed to remove — i.e. the lane freeze reports 'N rows reverted' while the rows are still live.
findings.affected: the canonical store during any automated lane freeze; both directions lose data (concurrent promote rows, or the reverted defect rows)
findings.evidence: lane_guard.py:76-77 `with open(store, encoding='utf-8') as f:` / `rows = [json.loads(line) for line in f if line.strip()]`; lane_guard.py:93-96 `backup = pfc._backup_path(store, 'lane_guard_revert')` / `pfc._fsynced_backup(store, backup)` / `pfc._atomic_write_rows(store, kept)`. `grep -n 'PromoteClaim|promote_lock|locked_store_rewrite' src/pilot/lane_guard.py` returns nothing across all 239 lines — the module imports `promote_final_cards as pfc` (lane_guard.py:40) and reuses its backup/write primitives but not its lock. Reachable from lane_spotcheck_tick.py:110 `code = lane_guard.run(ns)` with lane_spotcheck_tick.py:125 `--execute`.
findings.existing_test_gap: lane_guard.selftest (lane_guard.py:166) builds a temp store and asserts human_touched rows survive the revert; it never runs a second writer and never asserts that a claim is held, so the missing lock is invisible. store_write.selftest (store_write.py:177-183) proves a held claim blocks a rewrite — but only for callers that go through locked_store_rewrite, which lane_guard does not.
findings.fix_boundary: Wrap the read at :76 through the write at :96 in `PromoteClaim(store)`, or replace :93-96 with `store_write.locked_store_rewrite(store, kept, tag='lane_guard_revert')` after re-reading under the claim.

corrections: Three detail corrections, none fatal to the finding. (1) The store write is at lane_guard.py:99, not :96 — :94-95 are the backup, :96-98 the quarantine JSONL, :99 `pfc._atomic_write_rows(store, kept)`. The unguarded window is therefore :76-:99. (2) The scenario needs one precondition the write-up does not state: `revert_windows` returns early at :74 when `promoted_keys(records)` is empty, so the store is only rewritten when the day has `pwg.auto_promotion.v1` records — i.e. only under an active `--auto-promote-until` trial. There are currently 0 `*.PROMOTED.json` on disk and pc_lane_tick.cmd sets no `--auto-promote-until`, and the "PWG-RU spotcheck pc lane" task is registered Disabled and has never run (prod systemd unit documented NOT INSTALLED). The defect is real but latent until go-live steps 3+4 of pc_lane_tick.cmd's checklist are executed — hence P2 now, P1 the moment surveillance is enabled alongside the auto-promote trial. (3) The loss is not unrecoverable: :94-95 take a unique fsynced O_EXCL backup before the write, so the pre-write image survives; what is silently wrong is the freeze record's `rows_removed` count and the absence of any alert. Bonus wart found while tracing: `pfc._backup_path(store, 'lane_guard_revert')`'s second parameter is `merge`, used only as a truthiness test (`kind = 'premerge' if merge else 'legacy'`), so the 'lane_guard_revert' tag is discarded and lane_guard's backups are named `*.premerge.*.bak`, indistinguishable from a promote's own backups — its selftest asserts exactly that prefix.

Three corrections. (1) Line numbers drift: the backup/write block is :94-99, not :93-96 (`_backup_path` :94, `_fsynced_backup` :95, `_atomic_write_rows` :99). The quoted code text itself matches. (2) "Silently dropped" overstates the blast radius: `pfc._fsynced_backup(store, backup)` at :95 takes an O_EXCL, fsynced, collision-resistant copy of the exact pre-write on-disk bytes four lines before the replace, so a concurrent promote's rows are recoverable from `pwg_ru_translated.jsonl.premerge.<UTC>.p<pid>.<hex>.bak` — unnoticed, but not unrecoverable. Only a promote landing inside the narrow :95->:99 sub-window is lost outright. (3) The finding is net-new but should not be sold as contradicting the H2890 census: Uprava/data/integrity_tripwires.json:185-187 already records lane_guard verbatim — "Reviewed-preserving but NOT lock-held — no PromoteClaim anywhere in this file" — yet classes it `guarded: true`, because that census's `guarded` predicate is "a refuse-by-default gate protecting human-reviewed rows", not the concurrency lock. lane_guard is therefore absent from that census's list of four unguarded writers (audit_translation_provenance, pipeline_version, pwg_page_index, run_batch) by definition, not by oversight. Also worth noting for the fix: `pfc._backup_path(store, 'lane_guard_revert')` passes a string into a boolean `merge` parameter, so the revert's recovery artifact is named `.premerge.*` and is indistinguishable from a promoter backup.

findings.title: TM denylist has an asymmetric lock: denials are appended unlocked while unblocks do a locked read-modify-REPLACE, so a denial landing in the window is silently deleted
findings.invariant: The denylist is the only thing standing between a gate-rejected card/fragment and automatic TM reuse (translation_memory.py:266-268 raises DenylistError rather than tolerate a torn line, precisely so a denial can never be lost). Every writer of that file must therefore serialize against every other writer.
findings.failure_scenario: Audit lane EN calls `stamp_denylist_from_last_audit(keys=['brU~~a'])`, which appends a `kind: 'card'` denial row via a bare O_APPEND write at :368. Concurrently promote_final_cards.clear_denials_for_promotion calls `append_unblock`, which takes `_sidecar_lock` at :410, snapshots the file at :411 (`load_denylist(p)`), builds unblock rows, and at :424 calls `_atomic_extend_plain_jsonl` — which re-reads the file at :307-309 and `durable_replace`s the whole thing at :325. If the audit's append lands between :309 and :325, the replace overwrites it: the denial is gone, `stamp_denylist_from_last_audit` still returns n=1, and the next `load_tm`/`load_frag_tm` happily serves the defect translation the audit just rejected.
findings.affected: TM denial rows for defect-audited cards/fragments; a lost denial re-enables auto_exact reuse of gate-rejected translations across every subsequent generation run
findings.evidence: Unlocked writer: translation_memory.py:368 `append_jsonl_line(p, {... 'kind': 'card', 'address': address ...})` and :385 (the fragment twin) — no `_sidecar_lock` anywhere in `stamp_denylist_from_last_audit` (:335-397). Locked read-modify-replace: translation_memory.py:410 `with _sidecar_lock(p):` / :411 `denied = load_denylist(p)` / :424 `_atomic_extend_plain_jsonl(p, rows, ...)`, whose body reads the whole file at :307-309 `existing = fh.read()` and installs a new file at :325 `promotion_journal.durable_replace(tmp, path)`. window_common.append_jsonl_line (window_common.py:93-104) is a single O_APPEND `os.write` — tear-safe but with no defence against a concurrent whole-file replace. Both writers hit the same single global file (`denylist_path`, translation_memory.py:165-167 — no lang in the name), and the callers are different lanes: audit_window_en.py:570 and window_reports.py:557 stamp; promote_final_cards.py:345 unblocks.
findings.existing_test_gap: window_selftest.py:6786 and :7777 exercise append_unblock, and `_denylist_atomic_selftest` (translation_memory.py:1927) exercises the fault-injected replace, but all are single-process and sequential; no test ever appends a denial while an unblock holds the lock, so the asymmetry is untested.
findings.fix_boundary: Take `_sidecar_lock(p)` around the append loop in `stamp_denylist_from_last_audit` (translation_memory.py:365-397) — or, better, make every denylist writer go through `_atomic_extend_plain_jsonl` under `_sidecar_lock`, so the file has exactly one write discipline.

corrections: Severity should be P2, not P1. Two deflators, both measured rather than argued: (1) the exposure is a single ~2.6 ms read-to-replace window per promotion (measured on the live 29 KB sidecar), so a real hit needs an audit stamp landing inside it — my 119/300 loss rate came from 164 artificially stacked unblock cycles, not from a realistic single-promotion run; (2) the live denylist contains zero `unblock` rows and has not been written since 2026-07-06, so the promotion-side writer has not yet fired against the shared file in production — the loss is reachable but has not been realized. Also worth adding to the finding: on Windows the same race can instead abort `promotion_journal.durable_replace` with `PermissionError [WinError 5]` when the appender's O_APPEND handle is still open; `promote_final_cards.py:2216` catches that fail-open (loud warning, denials survive) while `coordinator.py:2159` journals and re-raises — so a minority of collisions are loud rather than silent. Two smaller corrections to the write-up: `window_reports.py`'s stamp call is at :565 (inside `_stamp_last_audit_denylist`, which begins at :535), not :557; and `requeue_from_audit.py:108` is a third unlocked appender the finding does not list — it is in fact the only one that produced the 107 live rows (`reason='requeue_all'`/`'requeue_defect'`), so the fix must cover it too, which the stated fix boundary (lock inside `stamp_denylist_from_last_audit`) does.

Two corrections to the finding as written. (1) The invariant is overstated: the denylist is NOT "the only thing standing between a gate-rejected card and automatic TM reuse" — translation_memory.py:341-344 documents it as a backstop behind the requeue path's forced `--no-tm`, for the case where the operator forgets the flag or bypasses requeue_from_audit. The correct invariant is the narrower, still-required one the repo declared P0 in CONCURRENCY_REAUDIT_2026-07-09.md: an appended denial row must never be silently dropped. (2) Reachability is weaker than claimed: `append_unblock` has never executed against the live denylist — 0 of 107 production rows are `kind: unblock`, and the `_sidecar_lock` file `translation_memory.denylist.jsonl.lock` (which the context manager creates unconditionally and never removes) does not exist, so the lock has never been taken there; both `_sidecar_lock` and `append_unblock` landed 2026-08-06 while the denylist's last write is 2026-07-06. Severity should be P2 (defence-in-depth hardening on a never-exercised path with a re-derivable payload), not P1. The proposed fix boundary is right as stated.

findings.title: make_edition_cut regenerates the interop artifacts only when ABSENT, so a sha256-pinned "immutable" edition can be cut over stale, pre-fix bytes
findings.invariant: An immutable edition manifest that pins a sha256 per file must pin bytes derived from the cards being released; the hash is a provenance claim, not a copy of whatever happened to be on disk.
findings.failure_scenario: `ensure_interop` computes `missing` and only shells out to export_interop when a file is absent. release/tei_lex0.xml, release/ontolex.ttl and release/reverse_index.jsonl are all committed to the repo, so `missing` is always empty and the exporter never runs. main() then copies those three files verbatim (line 149-150) and `manifest_files()` pins their sha256 (line 113) into release_manifest.json as an immutable, citable edition. Demonstrable staleness: the committed release/tei_lex0.xml contains three entries with the identical `xml:id="pwg-A"` and no `-2`/`-3` suffix anywhere (`grep -c 'xml:id="pwg-A-2"'` → 0), a shape the CURRENT export_tei cannot produce because of the `idn` counter at line 134. The artifact therefore predates the homograph fix, and `make_edition_cut edition_v1` would today pin the hash of pre-fix bytes while the manifest asserts `source_git_commit` = the current, fixed HEAD.
findings.evidence: make_edition_cut.py:96 `missing = [name for name in INTEROP if not os.path.exists(os.path.join(args.source_release, name))]` / :97 `if missing:` — no mtime, no cards-hash, no --force. make_edition_cut.py:149-150 `for name in INTEROP: copy_file(os.path.join(args.source_release, name), os.path.join(edition_dir, name))`. make_edition_cut.py:113 `files[rel] = {'sha256': sha256(path), 'bytes': os.path.getsize(path)}`.
findings.existing_test_gap: tests/test_make_edition_cut_lf_determinism.py covers copy_file/copy_tree/manifest_files line-ending determinism only (its four tests all operate on tmp_path fixtures). Nothing exercises ensure_interop, and nothing asserts that the copied interop bytes are derivable from args.cards. The LF test proves the hash is host-independent while saying nothing about whether it is content-correct.
findings.fix_boundary: make_edition_cut.py ensure_interop: regenerate unconditionally into a temp dir (or compare a hash of args.cards recorded alongside the artifacts) rather than testing os.path.exists; alternatively refuse to cut when the interop files are older than args.cards.

corrections: Three refinements, none of which touch the substance. (1) Line numbers are off by one in the evidence block: `missing = [...]` is make_edition_cut.py:95 (not 96), `if missing:` is :96 (not 97), and the verbatim copy loop is :148-149 (not 149-150). The sha256 pin at :113 is correct. (2) "The artifact predates the homograph fix" is true of the BYTES but not of the git history: this repo squashes one commit per PR, and both `release/tei_lex0.xml` and the `idn` counter were introduced in the same squashed commit 5869f25ee (2026-08-06, H2252 #1170) — the artifact was committed alongside the fix without being regenerated. The independent proof of staleness is the content itself (3 duplicate ids, 0 suffixes, unreproducible by HEAD) plus the live-checkout mtime, 2026-06-20, which is older than the cards file it claims to derive from (2026-07-13). (3) Impact is currently latent, not realized: no `release/edition_*` directory exists on disk or in git, and PRINT_DH_SPEED_REVIEW.md records "latest edition none" with G5/G6/G7/G10 still blocking. The defect would fire on the FIRST real cut, which the documented runbook triggers with no regeneration step — that latency is why I would not push this above P1, and why it should not be discounted below it either.

Three details need fixing, none fatal. (1) "the exporter never runs" is too strong — .github/workflows/ci.yml:403 passes `--source-release "$RUNNER_TEMP/release_fixture/source"` (a nonexistent dir), so CI does exercise ensure_interop, but only in the always-missing direction; the correct claim is that the exporter never runs on the DEFAULT `--source-release` (= repo release/), i.e. the production path. By the same token "Nothing exercises ensure_interop" in existing_test_gap is wrong as written — nothing exercises the SKIP path, which is the defective one. (2) "The artifact therefore predates the homograph fix" cannot be established from git: export_interop.py has exactly one commit in history (5869f25ee, 2026-08-06), the same commit that added the artifacts, so the exporter has never been modified post-commit. The staleness is instead proved by (a) the id shape and (b) filesystem mtimes in the live tree — artifacts 20-Jun, export_interop.py 4-Jul, assembled_cards.jsonl 13-Jul: the pinned bytes are ~3 weeks older than both the code and the cards they claim to derive from. (3) The evidence is stronger than the finding states: not just three `pwg-A` entries but 14,091 surplus colliding entries across 12,374 duplicated ids, and zero `-2` suffixes for ANY id in the file. Severity should be P2, not P1: G10 is "partial" with "real immutable edition cut still pending", no edition directory has ever existed, and recovery is deleting the edition dir and re-cutting after `export_interop.py all`.

findings.title: release_readiness computes the interop verdict, prints it, and then omits it from the edition blockers — G10 can read "ready-to-cut" on the same report whose G9 row reads "blocked"
findings.invariant: The G10 go/no-go verdict must be a function of every blocking gate the report itself evaluates; a gate that is measured and rendered but not counted is decoration.
findings.failure_scenario: `iok, imsg = interop_ok(args.release_dir)` (line 108) is used only to render the G9 table row (line 124). `eblockers = edition_blockers(blocking, rc, gc, double_exists)` (line 110) never receives `iok`, and edition_blockers (line 92-94) unions only the roadmap `blocking` list with local_gate_blockers. If validate_interop exits non-zero — corrupt/missing TEI, empty reverse index — and the roadmap's G9 row still says `"status":"passing"` (it does: quality_gates.jsonl:9), the report prints `| G9 interop artifacts | blocked | ... |` and, on the very next line, `| G10 edition cut | ready-to-cut | blockers=none |`, and `--fail-on-blocked` exits 0. Two further holes in the same function: G5 clears as soon as ONE row in the whole store is print-ready (`if review['print_ready'] == 0`, line 83), so 1 reviewed row out of 11,603 satisfies a blocks_print gate; and G7 clears on the mere EXISTENCE of gold/double_review_agreement.md (line 87-88, `os.path.exists`), so an empty file passes it. CI compounds this: ci.yml:401 invokes the script without --fail-on-blocked, so it can only ever exit 0.
findings.evidence: release_readiness.py:108 `iok, imsg = interop_ok(args.release_dir)` … :110 `eblockers = edition_blockers(blocking, rc, gc, double_exists)` (no iok argument). :92-94 `def edition_blockers(blocking, review, gold, double_exists): return sorted((set(blocking) - {G10}) | set(local_gate_blockers(review, gold, double_exists)))`. :83-84 `if review['print_ready'] == 0: blockers.append('G5_translation_store_review_gate')`. :87-88 `if not double_exists: blockers.append('G7_double_review_agreement')` with :109 `double_exists = os.path.exists(DOUBLE_REPORT)`.
findings.existing_test_gap: No test file references release_readiness. The only exercise is ci.yml:401, run against a one-card fixture release dir where validate_interop always succeeds, so the iok=False branch is never taken in any automated run.
findings.fix_boundary: release_readiness.py: pass iok into edition_blockers and append 'G9_schema_ci_interop' when false; raise the G5 predicate above a bare `== 0` (a ratio or an explicit expected count); make G7 assert the report's content, not its existence.

corrections: Two evidence details in the finding are wrong, and the severity is inflated from P1 to P2. (1) "CI compounds this: ci.yml:401 invokes the script without --fail-on-blocked, so it can only ever exit 0" understates the net: ci.yml:402 runs preflight_remaining_gates.py immediately after, which executes validate_interop as its own check (preflight_remaining_gates.py:224-225) and returns 1 whenever ANY check status is 'fail' (`failed = failed or status == 'fail'` :266, `return 1 if failed else 0` :274) — independent of --fail-on-blocked. So a broken interop DOES fail the workflow; release_readiness's exit 0 is not the last line of defence. A second net exists post-cut: validate_release.py re-parses tei_lex0.xml, greps ontolex:LexicalEntry, and re-checks reverse_index ru/key1 (:120-125). (2) "No test file references release_readiness" is false — RussianTranslation/tests/test_store_flags.py:65,88-91 imports it and pins review_counts()['print_ready']. The substantive gap survives (nothing tests edition_blockers or the G9/G10 interaction, and no automated run ever takes the iok=False branch), but the sentence as written is refuted. What the finding under-reports and I confirmed independently: preflight_remaining_gates.py:132-143 (edition_summary) has the IDENTICAL omission — its dashboard G10 row also prints "ready-to-cut" with interop broken — so the fix boundary must cover both files, not just release_readiness.py. Net: the human-facing go/no-go verdict is genuinely self-contradicting and reproducible, but no automated path silently ships a corrupt edition, hence P2 not P1.

Strike four claims. (a) "CI compounds this: ci.yml:401 invokes the script without --fail-on-blocked, so it can only ever exit 0" — misleading: ci.yml:400 runs validate_interop.py directly under `bash -e`, so a broken interop fails the job before release_readiness runs, and ci.yml:402's preflight_remaining_gates returns 1 on any failed check regardless of --fail-on-blocked. (b) "No test file references release_readiness" — false; tests/test_store_flags.py:65,78-95 imports it and pins review_counts(). (c) The G5 `print_ready == 0` predicate is not a hole: roadmap/print_review_minimum.json P0_G5 done_when is literally "print-ready rows are nonzero". (d) The G7 existence check is not a hole: P0_G7 done_when is literally "...and an agreement report exists". Both are gate-design choices in the roadmap, out of scope for a code-correctness finding. Add one omission the finding missed: preflight_remaining_gates.py:131-143 (`edition_summary`) has the identical gap — its dashboard G10 row also computes ready_to_cut without interop — so any fix must cover both files. Restate severity as P3: a human-facing display inconsistency reachable only after a human hand-flips G5/G6/G7 to "passing", with no programmatic consumer of the verdict and two independent nets (CI's direct validate_interop, validate_release's content re-checks) covering the real hazard.

findings.title: The DE edition graph stamps dct:license = Public Domain Mark 1.0 on the whole lexicon, contradicting its own pack licence (CC-BY-SA-4.0) and its own "project" rights posture for the NWS layer
findings.invariant: The machine-readable licence on a published RDF artifact must not be weaker than the rights the project actually holds or grants; a FAIR consumer reads dct:license, not the sidecar prose.
findings.failure_scenario: _ttl_vocab writes one blanket `dct:license <https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/>` on the `lime:Lexicon` node covering all five editions. Four lines later the same function emits `pwglex:rightsPosture "project"` for the NWS edition (LAYERS['nws'] at line 98 is `(..., 'project')`, not 'pd'). The shipped artifact shows both: release/fixture/de_edition/pwg_de_edition.ttl:25 carries the PD Mark, line 35 carries `pwglex:rightsPosture "project"` for `.../edition/nws`. Meanwhile the pack's own authored licence (release/pwg_de_sidecars/LICENSE-DATA, section 2) says the derived structure — the edition graph itself, government frames, form notes, citation edges, edition relations, the IRI scheme — is CC-BY-SA-4.0, and section 1 requires attributing Cologne for the 432 NWS senses; CITATION.cff:21 and .zenodo.json:22 both say `CC-BY-SA-4.0`, matching build_de_sidecar_pack.py:64 `DATA_LICENSE = 'cc-by-sa-4.0'`. A consumer who ingests only the .ttl (the normal case for a Zenodo RDF deposit) is told the whole graph is public domain with no attribution and no share-alike — the licence the project grants is lost on export. `dct:source` at line 311 is the same class of loss: the entire five-edition graph is attributed to the PWGScan URL alone.
findings.evidence: export_de_edition.py:311-312 `f.write('  dct:source <https://www.sanskrit-lexicon.uni-koeln.de/scans/PWGScan/> ;\n')` / `f.write('  dct:license <https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/> ;\n')`. export_de_edition.py:98 `'nws': ('NWS — Nachtragswörterbuch (Cologne working layer)', 'project'),`. Shipped: release/fixture/de_edition/pwg_de_edition.ttl:25 and :35. Contradicted by build_de_sidecar_pack.py:64 `DATA_LICENSE = 'cc-by-sa-4.0'` and release/pwg_de_sidecars/LICENSE-DATA §2 "DERIVED STRUCTURE — CC-BY-SA-4.0".
findings.existing_test_gap: export_de_edition --selftest (lines 757-914) asserts the rights fence in ONE direction only — that no Russian/forbidden field leaks OUT (assert_rights_safe probes at :897-907, quarantine counts at :830). Nothing asserts that the licence the graph declares matches the licence the pack grants, and build_de_sidecar_pack --selftest (:194-195) checks only that SHA256SUMS has 3 lines and ends with a newline. The two halves of the pack are never cross-checked.
findings.fix_boundary: export_de_edition.py _ttl_vocab: emit the CC-BY-SA-4.0 IRI for the lexicon (the derived structure) and move PD Mark to per-edition `dct:license` on the four `pd` editions only, leaving NWS with an attribution-required statement; make dct:source per-edition. Add a selftest asserting the emitted licence IRI equals build_de_sidecar_pack.DATA_LICENSE's IRI.

corrections: Two corrections, neither fatal. (1) Severity is inflated at P1; P2 is right. The error runs in the *under-claiming* direction — the project gives away its own copyleft rather than infringing anyone — the deposit ships LICENSE-DATA, README and DATASHEET stating the true two-layer posture, the Zenodo record-level licence is correct (cc-by-sa-4.0), and there is no proven RDF consumer: LOD_GRAPH.md:218-221 records that the w3id PURL is unregistered, so every IRI in the graph currently 404s and no SPARQL surface is published (the profile doc §1 assigns publication to csl-standards). The only third-party limb — Cologne attribution for NWS — covers 432 of 11,581 senses (3.7%) of markup over public-domain text. Real, shipped on a live DOI, worth fixing; not a P1. (2) The `dct:source` limb of the finding should be pared off: no contract requires per-edition sourcing, and the project has never modelled scan URLs for PW/SCH/PWKVN/NWS anywhere (a repo-wide grep of `scans/*` yields PWGScan and MWScan only), so "make dct:source per-edition" is a modelling improvement, not a violated invariant. (3) The `existing_test_gap` prose understates the pack selftest — build_de_sidecar_pack --selftest does more than count SHA256SUMS lines; at :203 it *asserts* `z['license'] == DATA_LICENSE`. That correction strengthens the finding: the correct licence string is already machine-asserted on one half of the pack while the other half emits a contradictory IRI with no assertion at all.

Three refinements, none fatal. (1) The finding calls release/fixture/de_edition/pwg_de_edition.ttl the "shipped artifact"; it is the committed fixture, and its sha256 (73edc64c...) does not match the pack's SHA256SUMS (9975ccc9...). The deposited .ttl is not in the repo at all - it was built from an untracked --art-dir. The finding still stands because the deposited manifest.json (459/11581, source_rows 11603) proves the full-store build ran through the same unconditional lines, which I reproduced. (2) The finding names only the TTL; the same PD Mark is also the ONLY licence statement in the TEI Lex-0 serialization, export_de_edition.py:596-598 -> output pwg_de_edition.tei.xml:8, where it at least carries the scope note "(19th-c. German editions)" that the TTL lacks. The fix boundary must cover both serializations. (3) I could not byte-reproduce the deposited ttl (my 2026-08-16 rebuild hashes 8a8fccee..., not 9975ccc9...), because the live store has changed since the deposit - so the reproduction is on today's store, not on the deposited bytes; the unconditional code path makes that immaterial to the claim.

findings.title: Orchestrator unit has no TimeoutStartSec: systemd kills a 600 s paid dispatch at the 90 s default
findings.invariant: A dispatch that the code bounds at PRODUCTION_HARD_TIMEOUT_MS (600 s per call, 720 s wrapper) must be allowed to run to its own bound; the supervisor must not impose a shorter, undeclared kill.
findings.failure_scenario: Timer fires -> `run-once` claims a manifest job and fans out up to 3-4 `run_claimed` workers, each bounded at DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S = HARD_TIMEOUT_MS//1000 = 600 s (headless_worker.py:67,74; execution_contract.py:93) under wrapper_timeout_s = +120 s (headless_worker.py:92,95). The unit declares Type=oneshot (line 7) and sets no `TimeoutStartSec=`, so systemd applies DefaultTimeoutStartSec (90 s on stock distros). At t=90 s systemd SIGTERMs the whole ExecStart, mid model call: the paid call is lost, the DB row stays state='in_progress' (cmd_run_once never reaches its release path at max_account_orchestrator.py:1130-1135), and the coordinator runtime reservation is left unreleased. Any per-call ceiling above 90 s is unreachable in production.
findings.evidence:
pwg-ru-max-orchestrator.service:6-12 `[Service]
Type=oneshot
User=pwg-factory
WorkingDirectory=...
ExecStart=... run-once` — no `TimeoutStartSec=`, no `RemainAfterExit=`. Against `execution_contract.py:93 PRODUCTION_HARD_TIMEOUT_MS = 600000` and `headless_worker.py:92 WRAPPER_TIMEOUT_HEADROOM_S = 120`.
findings.existing_test_gap: Nothing in ci.yml parses or lints the deploy/ units; the whole runtime-contract lane (ci.yml:235-272) exercises max_account_orchestrator's Python selftests, which run in-process and never see systemd. No test asserts that the unit's start timeout is >= the code's own hard timeout.
findings.fix_boundary: RussianTranslation/deploy/pwg-ru-max-orchestrator.service — add `TimeoutStartSec=` derived from wrapper_timeout_s(DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S); optionally a CI step that asserts the unit's timeout >= execution_contract.PRODUCTION_HARD_TIMEOUT_MS.

corrections: The finding's mechanism is inverted. "The unit declares Type=oneshot (line 7) and sets no `TimeoutStartSec=`, so systemd applies DefaultTimeoutStartSec (90 s on stock distros)" is false: systemd disables the start timeout for Type=oneshot precisely when no TimeoutStartSec=/TimeoutSec= is given (systemd.service(5); confirmed TimeoutStartUSec=infinity on every stock oneshot unit of the live box, whose DefaultTimeoutStartUSec is 90 s). Nothing in the unit imposes any ceiling — RuntimeMaxUSec, JobTimeoutUSec and JobRunningTimeoutUSec are all infinity too. The only true residue is cosmetic/defensive: adding an explicit `TimeoutStartSec=infinity` (or a value derived from wrapper_timeout_s) would make the intent legible and immune to a future edit that changes Type= away from oneshot or adds a drop-in `TimeoutSec=`. That is a P3 hardening nit, not a P1 lost-paid-dispatch bug. A related but separate and benign observation: with OnUnitActiveSec=15 against a possibly 720 s run, systemd simply will not restart the unit while it is active — no overlap, no defect.

The mechanism is wrong, not just mis-scoped: for Type=oneshot systemd disables the start timeout by default (TimeoutStartUSec=infinity), so DefaultTimeoutStartSec=90 s never applies and no SIGTERM occurs at t=90 s. Also, ExecStart run-once is line 11 (line 10 is `recover`), and the unit is not installed on the known prod host (no /opt/factory, no unit file), so the production premise is unverified. The only defensible residue is a P3 hardening note: pin TimeoutStartSec= explicitly so the unit stays safe if Type= is ever changed away from oneshot, or if a drop-in/manager default is later introduced.

findings.title: CI on master has been RED for three consecutive pushes at the cross-language parity gate, and two commits landed on top of the red

findings.title: The `gloss-langs` durable-metadata API returns only the first of a key1's records; 17,284 records are unreachable
findings.invariant: key1 does not identify a PWG record. `HEADER_RE` (line 39) captures the `<h>` homonym number as group(5), but `parse()` (lines 148-153) returns only groups 3 and 4 and discards it, so every consumer that joins on key1 alone has a non-injective key.
findings.failure_scenario: `python pwg_mask.py gloss-langs akza` walks records, matches the first record whose key1 == 'akza', prints a payload stamped `{"key1": "akza", "key2": ..., "gloss_lang_spans": [...]}` and returns (line 430). csl-orig has six akza records — homonyms 1, 2, 3 plus supplement columns at (1,1143), (1,1147), (5,945). The emitted sidecar covers homonym 1's body only, while claiming to be the gloss_lang metadata for the headword 'akza'. The docstring calls this the "durable metadata API" (line 415) and the module header advertises `gloss-langs <key1>` (line 21), so this payload is designed to be attached to a portrait/sidecar (gloss_lang_spans docstring, line 263). `cmd_card` (line 396-411) has the identical early `return`. Downstream, the {%…%} translate/mask decision is per-span, so a sidecar built this way asserts "no Latin/English braces" for homonyms whose bodies were never inspected.
findings.affected: 17,284 of 123,366 PWG records are invisible to `pwg_mask.py card` / `gloss-langs`; any sidecar built from them under-reports non-German brace spans for those bodies.
findings.evidence:
pwg_mask.py:148-153 —
    def parse(buf):
        m = HEADER_RE.match(buf[0])
        key1 = m.group(3) if m else ''
        key2 = m.group(4) if m else ''
        body = '\n'.join(buf[1:])
        return key1, key2, body       # group(5) — the <h> homonym number — dropped
pwg_mask.py:421-430 —
    for buf in records():
        key1, key2, body = parse(buf)
        if key1 == target:
            payload = {...}
            print(json.dumps(payload, ...)); return
Measured on csl-orig pwg.txt: 13,900 key1 values own more than one record, totalling 17,284 records that this lookup can never reach. Only 6,494 of 123,366 records carry <h>, so the missing number cannot be recovered downstream either.
findings.existing_test_gap: `_selftest()` (pwg_mask.py:435-519) exercises classify_pct_detail, gloss_lang_spans offsets, mask and restore entirely on synthetic in-memory strings — it never calls records()/parse()/cmd_card/cmd_gloss_langs, so no test has ever seen a key1 that owns two records.
findings.fix_boundary: pwg_mask.parse() must return the homonym (group 5), and cmd_card/cmd_gloss_langs must either take an optional `<h>` argument or emit all matching records rather than `return`ing on the first.

corrections: The invariant ("key1 is not injective; parse() drops the `<h>` group and the two CLI commands stop at the first match") is correct, and the counts 123,366 / 13,900 / 17,284 verify. Wrong is the blast radius: `cmd_gloss_langs` has zero callers anywhere in the repo (only its own dispatch table and a CLI mention in pwg_ru.md:220), so no sidecar is ever built from it and no downstream artifact under-reports non-German brace spans. The live gloss_lang path is export_de_edition.py:237, per-row on the row's own `de`, never keyed by key1; and microstructure.py:364-374 — the actual portrait/sidecar tool — already takes an optional `<h>` and prints all homonyms. `akza` has 9 records, not 6. Restated correctly this is: "the `pwg_mask.py card` / `gloss-langs` inspection CLIs silently show only the first of a headword's records, so a human debugging a homonym sees the wrong body" — P3 developer ergonomics, fixed by the same optional-`<h>` argument microstructure.py already uses.

findings.title: _stale_for emits one key1 and one input_raw_sha256 for an N-row group, so N-1 rows are re-checked against the wrong hash
findings.invariant: The drain contract (watch_upstream.py:18-21) is "the drain re-hashes the regenerated input and re-runs the mismatches" — so each flagged store line must be paired with ITS OWN stamped provenance.input_raw_sha256.
findings.failure_scenario: `load_promoted` (lines 113-128) buckets rows by `(cg.form_key(key1), layer)` and appends `(lineno, key1, input_raw_sha256)` per row. A single form_key+layer routinely holds several rows: dict_merge.py:41-48 documents that a headword's PWG per-preverb sub-cards (`~~h0_NN_<preverb>`) and folded Nachträge all share layer 'pwg'. `_stale_for` then emits `lines` for all N rows but takes `key1` and `input_raw_sha256` from `rows[0]` only. The drain regenerates input for the group, hashes it, compares against the single emitted sha, and concludes the whole group matches (or the whole group differs) on the strength of row 1's stamp. A sub-card whose input genuinely changed is judged unchanged and never re-translated — the exact failure the sha stamp exists to prevent — and the emitted `key1` is row 1's spelling, not the spelling of rows 2..N.
findings.affected: Every flagged headword whose form_key+layer owns more than one promoted store row — i.e. every headword with PWG preverb sub-cards or folded Nachträge.
findings.existing_test_gap: selftest() at watch_upstream.py:430-433 constructs `promoted` with exactly ONE row per (form_key, layer) — `{'pwg': [(10,'agni','SHA_A')], 'pw': [(11,'agni','SHA_B')]}` — and asserts `stale[0]['lines'] == [10]`. The multi-row-per-layer case, which is the normal case for PWG sub-cards, is never constructed.
findings.fix_boundary: watch_upstream._stale_for (lines 235-249): emit one entry per store row (or carry a parallel list of (lineno, key1, sha) triples) instead of collapsing to rows[0].

corrections: Two corrections. (1) The key1 half of the claim is refuted by real data: in the live 11,603-row store, 0 of 315 multi-row (form_key, layer) groups have more than one distinct key1 — form_key groups in this store are key1-homogeneous, so "the emitted key1 is row 1's spelling, not the spelling of rows 2..N" is false in practice. Only the sha collapses. (2) The failure_scenario overstates the consequence. "A sub-card whose input genuinely changed is judged unchanged and never re-translated" is not demonstrable: all N linenos are emitted in 'lines' (and counted in per_layer flagged_rows), and each store row carries its own provenance.input_raw_sha256, so no row is hidden from the drain and the correct per-row hash is available at the emitted lineno. The accurate statement is that the worklist's and the markdown report's sha column is unreliable for any multi-row group (e.g. form_key 'Ap': 93 rows, 35 distinct shas, one printed), which misleads a human reviewer and would mislead a future consumer that trusted it — a reporting defect, not a silent skip. The fix_boundary at _stale_for lines 235-249 and the selftest gap at 430-433 are both accurate as stated.

findings.title: The Nachträge adjacent-marker fix is applied only to the loci export; portrait() still misattributes ~2,310 back-references to sense 1
findings.invariant: Two consumers parsing the same PWG body must agree on which sense a citation belongs to. A PWG Nachträge back-reference glues its markers with no separating space (`1〉b〉 <ls>…</ls>`), and `MARK` (line 45) requires whitespace/em-dash/start before a marker, so the second marker is invisible to split_senses.
findings.failure_scenario: `leaf_senses` pre-inserts the missing space via `ADJACENT_MARKERS` (line 330) so the export sees `1〉 b〉` and assigns sense_id '1b'. `portrait()` (line 226-236) calls `split_senses(body)` on the raw body with no such pre-pass — deliberately, per the comment at lines 311-314 ("scoped to this export's own body copy only, never touching the shared split_senses/MARK used by sense_node/portrait elsewhere"). So for the same Nachträge record, `pwg_sense_loci.tsv` records the <ls> locus under sense '1b' while the lexicographic portrait — the artifact schemas/pwg_ru_lexicographic_portrait.schema.json describes and the one export_lod.de_card_senses re-derives from (export_lod.py:531-535) — files it under sense '1'. Downstream consumers joining kosha sense-reconciliation rows to portrait senses join a '1b' locus onto a '1' node.
findings.affected: ~2,310 PWG Nachträge back-references; their <ls> loci are attributed to the wrong sense in every portrait and in every DE edition sense derived from it via export_lod.
findings.evidence:
microstructure.py:315 —
    ADJACENT_MARKERS = re.compile(r'([)〉])(?=(?:\d{1,2}|[a-z])[)〉])')
microstructure.py:330 (export path only) —
        body = ADJACENT_MARKERS.sub(r'\1 ', '\n'.join(buf[1:]))
microstructure.py:228 (portrait path) —
        body = '\n'.join(buf[1:])
        senses = [sense_node(s) for s in split_senses(body)]
Measured on csl-orig pwg.txt: the ADJACENT_MARKERS pattern matches 2,310 times (the code comment at line 309 says 2,273 — same order of magnitude).
findings.existing_test_gap: The module has no selftest and no tests/ file; the only exercise of split_senses is via `cmd_sample`, which prints a portrait for the first 6 a-section records and is never asserted. Nothing compares the sense_id a body gets through leaf_senses against the one it gets through portrait, which is exactly the divergence.
findings.fix_boundary: microstructure.py: either apply ADJACENT_MARKERS inside split_senses (one shared normalisation), or relax MARK's lookbehind to accept a preceding `)`/`〉`. The comment's stated reason for scoping — avoiding a side effect on portrait — is the defect, not the mitigation.

corrections: Three corrections. (1) Mechanism mislabelled: the dominant shape is NOT a Nachtraege back-reference but an ordinary main-entry sub-sense opening, '<div n="1"> 1〉a〉 …' (Agraha, karzaRa, gavyu/, trita/, pUjana, bfhatPala). The code comment at microstructure.py:305-314 and CHANGELOG.md:2327 carry the same mislabel; the finding inherited it. (2) Count: regex match count is not impact count — 1,980 records (1.6% of 123,366) actually change sense tree, 1,705 with an <ls> in the newly split segment; not '~2,310 back-references'. (3) Blast radius: 'downstream consumers joining kosha sense-reconciliation rows to portrait senses' describes no existing consumer — kosha's pipeline never touches portraits and the RU store's sense_tag is not split_senses-derived. The accurate harm statement: portrait() and export_lod's German enrichment graph emit a structurally wrong sense tree (sub-sense 'a' merged into its parent, its <ls> loci attributed to the parent) for 1,980 records, and any future join against pwg_sense_loci.tsv would mis-key. Hence P3, not P2.
