findings.title: The auto-promote surveillance heartbeat is satisfied by an empty or content-free spot-check report, because only the filename prefix and the mtime are ever read
findings.invariant: H2264 / ARCHITECTURE §3: unsupervised auto-promotion into the canonical store may proceed only while live R4.1 surveillance (an actual spot-check over the day's promoted cards) exists.
findings.failure_scenario: `fresh_spotcheck` matches on filename prefix/suffix and `os.path.getmtime` only. It never opens the file, so it cannot distinguish (a) a real report, (b) a truncated/half-written report, (c) a report from a day with zero promotions — `spot_check_daily.build_report` returns `sampled: []`, `defects: []`, `sev3_count: 0` for an empty population (spot_check_daily.py:215-245), a vacuous clean — or (d) a literally empty JSON object. Any of these unlocks step 5b in nonstop_scheduler.tick (:299-307), and the lane runs `bounded_staged_run --auto-promote-until ...`, promoting machine output into `pwg_ru_translated.jsonl` with no defect surveillance behind it. lane_guard.evaluate (:60-64) then reads `report.get('sev3_count') or 0` on the same vacuous report and returns no-freeze, so the halt rule cannot fire either.
findings.evidence: lane_spotcheck_tick.py:64-74 `if not (name.startswith('spotcheck_') and name.endswith('.json')): continue` / `age = now - os.path.getmtime(path)` / `if age <= max_age and (best is None or age < best[0]): best = (age, path)` — no `json.load`, no schema/date/population check. Consumer: nonstop_scheduler.py:301-307 `fresh = lane_spotcheck_tick.fresh_spotcheck(cfg['telemetry_dir']); if not fresh: return done('skip', ...)` else the tick proceeds to `runners.bounded_run`.
findings.existing_test_gap: nonstop_scheduler selftest case (8e) at nonstop_scheduler.py:515-521 literally writes `f.write('{}')` into `spotcheck_2026-08-03.json` and then ASSERTS `rec8e['verdict'] == 'window'` — the test encodes the hole as intended behaviour. lane_spotcheck_tick's own selftest (:182-188) checks only freshness/staleness/absent-dir, never content validity.
findings.fix_boundary: lane_spotcheck_tick.fresh_spotcheck — load the JSON and require `schema == spot_check_daily.SCHEMA`, a `date` inside the freshness window, and a non-vacuous population/sampled set before returning the path; keep the mtime check as a cheap pre-filter.

corrections: One half of the proposed fix survives as cheap hardening, and it is worth recording even though the finding as written is refuted: `telemetry/` lives inside the `pwg-ru-data` git checkout and `nonstop_scheduler.Runners.commit_telemetry` (:225-237) commits and pushes it, so spotcheck reports are git-tracked. Any fresh clone or a `git pull` that updates those files re-stamps their mtime to checkout time, and `fresh_spotcheck` would then read an arbitrarily old report as live surveillance. Comparing the report's own `date` field (and `schema == spot_check_daily.SCHEMA`) against the freshness window costs one `json.load` and closes that, and unlike the population check it does not break the documented bootstrap — a day-0 report carries today's date. The finding's other three sub-scenarios ((b) truncation, (d) `{}`) and its population/sampled requirement should not be carried forward: (b) is precluded by the atomic `.tmp` + `os.replace` write, (d) has no production writer, and (c) is the intended unlock. Severity is P3 hardening, not P1: nothing has ever run this path, and the primary promotion gate is independent.

Three sub-claims are wrong or overstated and should be trimmed. (1) "(b) a truncated/half-written report" cannot come from the production writer: spot_check_daily.main writes to `out + '.tmp'` and then os.replace (:277-283), and `spotcheck_<date>.json.tmp` does not end in `.json`, so fresh_spotcheck never sees a partial write (and *.tmp is gitignored in pwg-ru-data). Truncation needs a foreign/manual copy. (2) "(c) a report from a day with zero promotions — a vacuous clean" is not by itself a hole: a zero-population report is honest evidence that the daily job DID run, which is exactly what the gate ("surveillance is LIVE") asks; the genuine vacuity risk is a mis-pointed --records-dir yielding population=0 while promotions happen, which is a different defect. (3) "lane_guard.evaluate then reads the same vacuous report and returns no-freeze, so the halt rule cannot fire" mis-describes the chain: in the daily job lane_spotcheck_tick.tick (:106-112) hands lane_guard the report spot_check_daily just wrote in the same process, never the foreign file the scheduler matched; evaluate() only sees a garbage report if a human runs lane_guard.py --spotcheck by hand. The load-bearing, reproducible half is the first one — fresh_spotcheck is content-blind and mtime-only. Also add the stronger real-world trigger the finding misses: because telemetry/ is git-tracked and commit_telemetry does `git add -A`, any clone or checkout of pwg-ru-data refreshes the mtime of every archived spotcheck report, so a genuinely dead surveillance job passes the 48h gate for 48h after a deploy — which is why the fix_boundary's "date inside the freshness window" check matters more than the schema check.

findings.lead_adjudication: Correctness REFUTED the framing and it is right to: the module docstring, CHANGELOG 1.141.8 and the go-live checklist all describe `fresh_spotcheck` as a HEARTBEAT — 'is the daily surveillance job scheduled and running' — not as a verdict, and R4.1's teeth are `lane_guard`'s `lane_freeze_<lane>.json`, which `nonstop_scheduler.tick` step 1 checks before ever reaching this branch. So the title's 'gate goes green on corrupt cards' is wrong and is struck. But reproduction CONFIRMED something the correctness lens did not address: driving the real `fresh_spotcheck` in a temp dir, it accepted a 0-byte file, a truncated `{"schema": "pwg.spot` fragment, and a `{}` named `spotcheck_2026-01-01.json`; and the real `nonstop_scheduler.tick()` then returned verdict='window' with a spy showing the production runner would be spawned with `--execute --auto-promote-until`. A heartbeat that a `touch` on an empty file satisfies is not evidence that surveillance ran. Ruling: CONFIRMED at P2, retitled to the heartbeat claim, with the false-green-on-cards claim removed. The repo's own selftest at nonstop_scheduler.py:517-522 writes `'{}'` and asserts the window proceeds, so the behaviour is encoded as intended and this is a contract weakness rather than a bug.

findings.title: verb_worklist reads a worktree-local store, so already-promoted roots are re-queued as un-translated
findings.invariant: There is exactly ONE logical pwg_ru store per checkout tree; any consumer that decides what still needs translating must resolve it through `store_path.canonical_store` (env override → main-worktree store → local), the documented H255/H805 loss-mode fix.
findings.failure_scenario: verb_worklist.py hard-codes `STORE = os.path.join(RT, 'src', 'pwg_ru_translated.jsonl')` and never imports store_path, so it honours neither `$PWG_RU_STORE` nor the main-worktree redirect. Run inside a linked worktree (the sanctioned isolation path in this repo's CLAUDE.md) the file does not exist, `store_roots` hits `if not os.path.exists(path): return done` (:54) and returns an empty set, so `done` is empty, `remaining = [k for k in attested if k not in done]` (:76) contains every DCS-attested root including the ~48 already promoted, `done_promoted` is written as `[]`, and `verb_batch_worklist.json` — the drain queue other tools consume — presents finished roots as outstanding work. The sibling `nominals_worklist.py` does the same job correctly (`STORE = canonical_store(STORE)`, :56), so the two worklists disagree about what is done.
findings.evidence: verb_worklist.py:30 `STORE = os.path.join(RT, 'src', 'pwg_ru_translated.jsonl')`; :52-55 `def store_roots(path=STORE): done = set(); if not os.path.exists(path): return done`; :74-76 `done = store_roots(store)` / `remain = sorted((k for k in attested if k not in done), ...)`. Contrast nominals_worklist.py:52,56 `from store_path import canonical_store` / `STORE = canonical_store(STORE)` with the comment "the runnable/promoted counts must be read from the SAME store a worktree drain promotes into (H255 w06 loss / H805)".
findings.existing_test_gap: No test file references verb_worklist and it has no `--selftest`; `.github/workflows/ci.yml` never invokes it. Nothing asserts that a worklist generator resolves the store through canonical_store, so the one module that skipped the H805 fix is invisible to CI.
findings.fix_boundary: verb_worklist.py — import `store_path.canonical_store` and wrap STORE exactly as nominals_worklist.py:56 does; optionally make `store_roots` raise instead of returning an empty set when the resolved path is missing.

corrections: Two corrections. (1) Mechanism/order: the failure cannot present as a silently wrong worklist in a linked worktree — build_worklist loads PREVERB (a sibling PWG clone, outside the repo) and the gitignored MANIFEST before it ever calls store_roots, so a worktree run dies with FileNotFoundError. The silent empty-`done` branch requires a tree where the manifest (and PWG) were provisioned but the store was not; the "run inside a linked worktree" reproduction as written is wrong. (2) Prior art / severity: the defect is already recorded verbatim at this line in RussianTranslation/pwg_ru/h1339/H1339_TIER_B_STATUS_2026-07-19.md (19-07-2026), and the only affected artifact is the gitignored, regenerable, explicitly "advisory / safe" verb_batch_worklist.json — no store write, no H255-class loss. P2 → P3.

findings.title: Nominal worklist's verb-exclusion list silently empties outside the main checkout, queueing verbs into the nominal drain
findings.invariant: Module contract (docstring :12-14): "Verb lemmas in a core ... are NOT queued here — they belong to the standing verb drain (H151). They are counted and set aside so the coverage report is honest, never silently dropped."
findings.failure_scenario: `PREVERB` is resolved two levels above the checkout (`RT/../../PWG/verbs01/pwg_preverb1.txt`, :42), so it only exists when the repo sits directly under the GitHub/ root. Verified in this worktree: the expression yields `C:\Users\user\Documents\PWG\verbs01\pwg_preverb1.txt` (exists: False) while the real file is at `C:\Users\user\Documents\GitHub\PWG\verbs01\pwg_preverb1.txt`. `verb_universe` then returns an empty set instead of raising, so `is_verb = (m.get('pos') == 'v') or (w in verbs)` (:122) collapses to the optional `.tsv` POS column alone — and that sidecar is itself optional (`if os.path.exists(tsv)`, :73). With both absent every verb lemma falls through into `hits`/`runnable_remaining` and gets queued for paid nominal translation, while the report prints `core_verbs_deferred_to_H151: []` and `core_verbs_count: 0` as if the core contained no verbs. The identically-named function in verb_worklist.py:42-49 has no existence check and would crash loudly in the same situation, so the silent copy is the divergence.
findings.evidence: nominals_worklist.py:83-86 `def verb_universe(path=PREVERB): roots = set(); if not os.path.exists(path): return roots`; :42 `PREVERB = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(RT, '..', '..', 'PWG', 'verbs01', 'pwg_preverb1.txt'))`; :120-124 `is_verb = (m.get('pos') == 'v') or (w in verbs); if is_verb: core_verbs.append(w); continue`; :174 `'core_verbs_deferred_to_H151': sorted(core_verbs)`.
findings.existing_test_gap: nominals_worklist has no selftest, no tests/ reference and no CI invocation, so nothing asserts that the exclusion universe is non-empty. The report writer (`write_report`, :216) prints `core verbs → verb drain (H151) | 0` without any "universe unavailable" marker, so even a human reading the committed coverage table cannot tell the list was never loaded.
findings.fix_boundary: nominals_worklist.verb_universe — drop the silent `os.path.exists` short-circuit (match verb_worklist.py:42-49) or return an explicit unavailable sentinel that build_worklist records as `verb_universe_unavailable: true` and refuses to emit a worklist on.

corrections: The guard divergence from verb_worklist.py is factually there, but the consequence chain is wrong at every link. PREVERB and dict_merge.V02 share the same GitHub/-root anchor, so the "silent" empty universe is perfectly correlated with a missing PWG corpus — which produces zero hits and zero runnable, not extra paid queueing. And build_worklist dies loudly on the gitignored `output/scale_manifest.freq.json` (line 109) before reaching the PWG index at all, so no relocated checkout can emit a worklist of any shape. Additionally, the `.tsv` sidecar is not effectively optional: extract_lexical_cores.py always writes it and all three committed cores carry a populated `pos` column, so pos-only exclusion already catches 98% of the verbs. At most this is a P3 hardening nit — add the missing-file raise (or a `verb_universe_unavailable` flag) for symmetry with verb_worklist.py.

findings.title: Coverage report prints 0% corpus/dictionary coverage when the sources are simply not built
findings.invariant: FL7 (stated at corpus_gate.py:113-130 and :391-399): "an absent evidence jsonl was silently skipped, so 'no independent gloss' could mean EITHER 'sources not built' OR 'this headword is genuinely uncovered' — indistinguishable". The fix must apply wherever that distinction is reported, not only in build_card.
findings.failure_scenario: `cmd_coverage` calls the back-compatible wrapper `corpus_examples`, which throws the status away (`return corpus_examples_with_status(slp1, limit)[0]`, :425-427). With `SamudraManthanam/web/corpus.db` absent (the normal state of a fresh clone or a linked worktree) every call returns `[]` with status `db_absent`, so `corp_hit` is 0 and the report prints "corpus signal (random sample of 300): 0 had >=1 aligned verse (0.0%)" — a measured-looking zero that actually means "the database was never opened". The same hole is one level up: `load_index` skips absent `koch/kna/fri/smirnov/kow.jsonl` (:136-138) and `cmd_coverage` never consults `evidence_status()` (:130), so the whole per-source coverage table reads 0.0% for every dictionary when `build_src.py` has not been run. These numbers are the input to the "is this headword uncovered" judgement that routes cards to the LLM verdict lane.
findings.evidence: corpus_gate.py:659 `corp_hit = sum(1 for k in corp_keys if corpus_examples(k, 1))`; :425-427 `def corpus_examples(slp1, limit=3): """Back-compatible list-only wrapper...""" return corpus_examples_with_status(slp1, limit)[0]`; :671-672 prints the percentage unconditionally. Compare :393-399, where the same statuses are preserved precisely because "before this, every one of these returned a bare [] indistinguishable from 'no matches', so a build/query failure silently read as 'word uncovered'".
findings.existing_test_gap: corpus_gate.py has no selftest of its own for coverage (only corpus_gate_sinonimy_selftest.py, which covers the sinonimy index), no tests/ file references it, and it is absent from .github/workflows/ci.yml — so no test ever runs cmd_coverage with the corpus DB or the dictionary jsonl files missing, which is exactly the state CI would be in.
findings.fix_boundary: corpus_gate.cmd_coverage — use `corpus_examples_with_status` and report `db_absent`/`db_error` as a distinct outcome instead of folding it into the miss count; print `evidence_status()` and the `SOURCES_PRESENT` set alongside the per-dictionary table, and suppress the percentage entirely when the source is absent.

corrections: Two corrections. (1) The blast-radius sentence "These numbers are the input to the 'is this headword uncovered' judgement that routes cards to the LLM verdict lane" is false. `cmd_coverage` only prints; nothing parses its stdout, and IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md:426 and :467 state explicitly that coverage "only prints aggregate percentages — it is not a key-picker". Card routing goes through `build_card`, which at :526 and :538 already keeps `corpus_stat` and `evidence_status()`. So this is a human-facing diagnostic misreport, not a routing defect — P3, not P2. (2) The failure_scenario understates the live trigger: it says the DB is "absent (the normal state of a fresh clone)", but in the actual live store today the file EXISTS at 0 bytes, so the path taken is `db_error` (not `db_absent`) — sqlite raises `no such table: corpus_lines` on all 300 queries, the stderr warning fires but the wrapper still returns `[]`, and stdout reports 0.0% against a documented 14–15%. The fix boundary must therefore cover `db_error`, not just `db_absent`.

findings.title: Re-glue skeleton drops a translated PWG sense on a normalised-tag collision, and the byte-identity gate cannot see it
findings.invariant: The re-glue is a lossless presentation of the layered store: every PWG sense row for a headword appears exactly once in the emitted card (success criterion (a), "zero re-translation", :14-16 and :231-232).
findings.failure_scenario: The skeleton is built as a dict keyed by `normalize_sense_tag(sense_tag)` per homonym. Two PWG rows in the same homonym slot whose tags normalise to the same string — `'1)'` and `'1.'`, or (more reachable) two distinct PWG sub-cards for the same headword that carry no `~~h\d+` marker and therefore both land in the `h0` bucket via `homonym_of` (:64-66, default `"h0"`) with sense tags `1,2,3...` — collide, and the later assignment overwrites the earlier. The first row's `pwg_ru` translation vanishes from the card and from the .md render. `stats['pwg_senses']` is computed as `sum(len(hv['senses']) ...)` (:174) — the post-collapse count — so the summary reports the reduced number as if it were the truth, and the `byte_ok` gate (:233-245) only asserts that each EMITTED `ru` exists in the store, which a dropped row trivially satisfies. PILOT_SUMMARY.tsv records `OK`.
findings.evidence: build_reglue.py:122-123 `h["senses"][normalize_sense_tag(st)] = {"sense": st, "pwg_ru": d.get("ru", ""), "supplements": []}` — plain dict assignment, no collision check; :64-66 `def homonym_of(subcard): m = re.search(r"~~(h\d+)", subcard or ""); return m.group(1) if m else "h0"`; :233-245 `store_ru = {r.get("ru", "") for r in recs}` … `if s["pwg_ru"] not in store_ru: bad += 1` (membership only, never a count or a coverage check); :245 `byte_ok = (bad == 0)`.
findings.existing_test_gap: There is no test for build_reglue anywhere in tests/ and it is not invoked by .github/workflows/ci.yml. `edition_rel.normalize_sense_tag` has its own idempotence/no-false-merge reasoning (edition_rel.py:229-257) but nothing asserts the consumer's key space is injective, and the only self-check in build_reglue is the membership-based `byte_ok`, which is blind to deletion by construction.
findings.fix_boundary: build_reglue.reglue_one — detect an existing key before assignment and either disambiguate (append the raw tag / a running ordinal) or fail loud; separately, strengthen the `main` gate to compare the emitted PWG-sense count against the number of non-correction pwg rows for the headword rather than only checking membership.

corrections: Two corrections of detail. (1) Mechanism: the `'1)'`-vs-`'1.'` normalisation collision is real but marginal; the dominant, actually-realized collision is many per-preverb PWG sub-cards inside the SAME homonym (`g_a~~h0_00_pwg00`, `g_a~~h0_02_ati`, `g_a~~h0_04_a_di` …) each restarting its own `1,2,3…` numbering — these sub-cards DO carry `~~h0`/`~~h1` markers, so the "default h0 bucket via homonym_of" framing is wrong; they collide within a correctly-identified homonym. (2) Blast radius is far larger than "a sense": 51% of PWG bodies are dropped for `gA` (63/123) and 75% for `DA` (244/326), and 757 rows across the 15-headword pilot — which is why I put severity at P1 rather than P2. Bounding factor kept: the layered store is untouched and canonical, and the damage is confined to the derived 15-headword pilot presentation, not a shipped user surface.

findings.title: is_sanskrit gates on a diacritic, so undiacriticized Sanskrit in {%…%} is sent to the German→Russian translator
findings.invariant: The module's own contract (compile_translatable.py:12-14): 'Sanskrit, sigla and grammar are NEVER translated (the project's format invariant); only the natural-language gloss is.' A `{%…%}` span in a PW/SCH/PWKVN layer that holds a Sanskrit headword must land in `keep` with `lang: ['sa']` and empty `text`; a German gloss must land in `text` with `lang: ['de']`.
findings.failure_scenario: `is_sanskrit` requires BOTH `IAST_ONLY.match` (lowercase Latin + IAST diacritics only) AND `SA_DIA.search` (at least one of āīūṛṝḷḹṅñṭḍṇśṣṃḥ). A Sanskrit lemma with no diacritic at all — `anna`, `deva`, `dharma`, `gata`, and the module's own HK/SLP1-style keys such as `aMSa`, `kenamsena` — fails the SA_DIA half and falls through to line 198, which unconditionally tags it `'lang': ['de'], 'text': g`. It then appears in the translatable manifest as German prose to render into Russian, so the translator invents a Russian gloss for a Sanskrit word that had to stay verbatim. Verified mechanically against the two regexes: is_sanskrit('anna')=False, ('deva')=False, ('dharma')=False, ('aMSa')=False, while ('kāma')=True. The inverse direction fires too — is_sanskrit('anteil an ṛta')=True, so an all-lowercase German gloss containing one Sanskrit diacritic is routed to `keep` with `'text': ''` and is never translated, i.e. silent loss of a translatable unit.
findings.affected: Every PW / SCH / PWKVN {%…%} span in the compiled translatable manifests under src/pilot/translate/*.json — `run_all()` (compile_translatable.py:252-300) processes every headword in the input dir, and the manifests feed the merged-translate lane (pwg_ru_prompts/6_merged_translate.md:78,189).
findings.evidence: compile_translatable.py:103-110 — `# a {%…%} span that is purely lowercase IAST (a Sanskrit headword like aṃśa,` / `# kenāṃśena) is NOT a German gloss — keep it verbatim, never translate it` / `IAST_ONLY = re.compile(r'^[a-zāīūṛṝḷḹṅñṭḍṇśṣṃḥ/\-\s]+$')` / `SA_DIA = re.compile(r'[āīūṛṝḷḹṅñṭḍṇśṣṃḥ]')` / `def is_sanskrit(span):` / `    return bool(IAST_ONLY.match(span.strip()) and SA_DIA.search(span))`. Routing at compile_translatable.py:194-198 — `if is_sanskrit(g):                       # Sanskrit headword in {%…%}, keep verbatim` / `    U.append({'layer': code, 'ref': '', 'lang': ['sa'], 'text': '', 'keep': [g]})` / `    continue` / `U.append({'layer': code, 'ref': '', 'lang': ['de'], 'text': g, 'keep': []})`. Note the comment itself names `kenāṃśena` — the diacritic-free spelling `kenamsena` that the same store uses as a key1 is classified German.
findings.existing_test_gap: There is no test file for compile_translatable.py anywhere under RussianTranslation/tests/ (the directory holds 21 test modules; none imports it), and the module ships no --selftest. tests/test_metalanguage_flags.py covers the sibling German-apparatus detector (classify_german_metalanguage) but not the Sanskrit-vs-German split in this module. The inverse half of this defect was already noted once in RussianTranslation/CODE_REVIEW_2026-07-04.md:87 ('IAST_ONLY can drop a German gloss containing one diacritic') and was never fixed; the undiacriticized-Sanskrit direction is not recorded there.
findings.fix_boundary: compile_translatable.py:109-110 — replace the diacritic requirement with a positive Sanskrit test (the shared sanskrit_util shim already present at src/sanskrit_util.py, or a SLP1/HK-shape check plus the layer's own key1), and make the German branch at :198 reject a span that is a single token equal to the card's headword.

corrections: Two corrections. (1) The "affected" field is overstated: `run_all()` does write the manifests, but nothing in the codebase consumes them — the merged-translate lane reference at pwg_ru_prompts/6_merged_translate.md:78,189 is prose guidance to a translator agent, not a data dependency, and the automated production lane (gen_opt_harness2 → pwg_mask → headless_worker) never touches compile_translatable. Consequently there is no shipped corruption: 0 of 5,577 pw/sch/pwkvn store rows show the defect. Severity should be P3, not P2. (2) The inverse direction ("is_sanskrit('anteil an ṛta')=True → silent loss of a translatable unit") is true as a regex fact but does not fire on real data — all 25 multiword `sa`-tagged spans in the 12,163 manifests are genuine Sanskrit citations, so no German gloss was actually swallowed. Drop the inverse half from the finding; it is also already knowingly accepted at CODE_REVIEW_2026-07-04.md:86. The forward direction (424 undiacriticized Sanskrit headwords tagged `de`) is genuinely new and correctly stated, and the fix_boundary at :109-110 is the right place.

findings.title: prompt_rule_audit --fail-on-missing exits 0 when the audited prompt template is absent
findings.invariant: The 14 entries of RULES (prompt_rule_audit.py:247-337) are the manual-derived translation rules — Apresjan discrimination, Hartmann equivalence_type, the samāsa/compound rule, the correlatives rule, the H1305 Russian-style rules (NO LETTER Ё, «вм.», «в знач.», ed. Bomb.) — that must be physically present in the shipped prompt. `--fail-on-missing` is documented as the build-time contract check (prompt_rule_audit.py:29-31, docs/manuals/RUSSIANTRANSLATION_DEEP_MANUAL.md:408 `python src\pilot\prompt_rule_audit.py --fail-on-missing`). A non-zero exit must mean 'the prompt no longer carries a required rule'; a zero exit must mean 'it does'.
findings.failure_scenario: `missing_rules` is summed over `scanned`, which is filtered to targets where `exists` is true (:992-993). If src/pilot/run_pilot_wf.js is renamed, moved, or lost — the very file whose `const TR` block IS the production `translation` prompt segment (gen_opt_harness2.py:699-706) — then `targets` has one entry with `exists: False`, `scanned` is empty, and `missing_rule_count` is 0. `missing_files` is computed (:994) and surfaced in the JSON report, but the exit gate at :1054 tests only `prompt_report['missing_rule_count']`. The command prints `MISSING FILE ...` and exits 0. A CI or pre-window step keyed on the exit code reports the rule contract satisfied while zero rules were actually checked. The generated harness path is already conditional (`if os.path.exists(harness): paths.append(harness)`, :1029-1031), so the template is the only target that can carry the check, and its absence is precisely the case that silently empties the denominator.
findings.affected: The build-time prompt-rule contract for every RU window; a false green here means a window can ship with the Apresjan/Hartmann/compound/correlative/ru-style rules silently absent from the prompt.
findings.evidence: prompt_rule_audit.py:991-1000 — `targets = [audit_text(path) for path in paths]` / `scanned = [target for target in targets if target['exists']]` / `missing_rules = sum(len(target['missing']) for target in scanned)` / `missing_files = [target['path'] for target in targets if not target['exists']]` ... `'missing_rule_count': missing_rules,` / `'missing_files': missing_files,`. prompt_rule_audit.py:887-889 — `def audit_text(path):` / `    if not os.path.exists(path):` / `        return {'path': path, 'exists': False, 'rules': [], 'missing': []}`. The gate: prompt_rule_audit.py:1054 `if args.fail_on_missing and prompt_report['missing_rule_count']:` — `missing_files` is never consulted for the exit code.
findings.existing_test_gap: No test module under RussianTranslation/tests/ imports prompt_rule_audit, and the module has no --selftest. Nothing exercises build_report with a non-existent target path, so the zero-denominator case has never been executed under assertion.
findings.fix_boundary: prompt_rule_audit.py:1054 — make the gate `if args.fail_on_missing and (prompt_report['missing_rule_count'] or prompt_report['missing_files']):`, and/or have build_report count a missing required target as len(RULES) missing rules rather than 0.

corrections: Two detail corrections. (a) RULES holds 15 entries, not 14, and spans :247-338. (b) The finding under-states the blast radius in one direction and over-states it in another: it misses that the same zero-denominator flows through the LIVE in-process gate, audit_window.run_prompt_semantic_audit:311-353, which returns returncode 0 instead of 2 and prints "Prompt/manual rules: PASS" — so the fix boundary should cover audit_window.py:321 as well as prompt_rule_audit.py:1054; but the "a window can ship with the rules silently absent" framing is too strong, because run_pilot_wf.js is git-tracked and its absence makes gen_opt_harness2.py:700 read_text raise before any generation, so the realistic harm is a safety net that cannot detect the loss of its own only target (harness is gitignored and absent), not a silent bad ship. Hence P3, not P2.

findings.title: fix_german_connectives --store rewrites German phrases inside «…» verbatim quotes that its own detector deliberately masks out
findings.invariant: The module states the fence twice. Docstring (:10-13): 'Substitutions apply ONLY to free text — never inside retained markup ({%German%}, {#Sanskrit#}, <ab>/<ls>/<is>) or inside «…» verbatim German quotes (which a corrigendum may be pointing at and must keep).' Comment (:70-74): the patterns 'are imported from german_residue_scan so the detector and the fixer can never drift'. Detector and fixer must therefore agree on which spans are in scope.
findings.failure_scenario: german_residue_scan detects MIT_ERGAENZUNG and FEHLERHAFT_FUER on `masked` — text with `{%…%}`, `{#…#}`, `«…»`, `<ab|ls|is|lex>` spans overwritten by spaces (german_residue_scan.py:159, 169, 171). fix_ru_store applies those same two patterns with `.subn` on the FULL, unmasked text (fix_german_connectives.py:122-123), before the masking helper `_sub_free_only` is used for the lone connectives at :128. So a row whose `ru` field contains a preserved German corrigendum quote — e.g. «… mit Ergänzung von …», the exact category the docstring says must be kept and that the scanner's own selftest fixture models with «nahe stehend» (german_residue_scan.py:257) — is silently rewritten to «… с восполнением …». The scanner reports zero hits for that row (the span was masked), so the change appears in no report; run_store then commits it through `locked_store_rewrite` (:171). The verbatim quote a corrigendum points at is destroyed and there is no per-row diff to recover it from — only the one-shot `.h1302.bak`, which is written only `if not os.path.exists(bak)` (:163), so a second campaign has no pre-state copy of its own.
findings.affected: Any row in pwg_ru_translated.jsonl whose `ru` field preserves a German phrase 'mit Ergänzung von' or 'fehlerhaft für' inside `«…»`, `{%…%}`, or a paired `<ab|ls|is|lex>` span, whenever `fix_german_connectives.py --store` is run without --dry-run.
findings.evidence: fix_german_connectives.py:120-128 — `n = 0` / `# 1) context-sensitive subs on the FULL text (tags intact, needed by the patterns).` / `text, c = MIT_ERGAENZUNG.subn('с восполнением', text); n += c` / `text, c = FEHLERHAFT_FUER.subn('ошибочно вместо', text); n += c` / `text, c = CITATION_ZU.subn(r'\1к\2', text); n += c` / `text, c = CITATION_BEI.subn(r'у\1', text); n += c` / `text, c = MIT_HEADER.subn('С', text); n += c` / `# 2) lone connectives in free text only (protected spans masked).` / `text, c = _sub_free_only(text, LONE_STORE, SCAN_PROTECTED); n += c`. Detector side, german_residue_scan.py:159 `masked = mask_protected(text)` and :169-172 `for m in MIT_ERGAENZUNG.finditer(masked):` / `add(m.start(), m.end(), m.group(0), 'mit_ergaenzung', 0)` / `for m in FEHLERHAFT_FUER.finditer(masked):`. (CITATION_ZU/CITATION_BEI/MIT_HEADER are detected on the raw `text` at :166/:173/:175, so those three are consistent — the drift is confined to the two phrase rules.) The protected set that both should share: german_residue_scan.py:55-63 PROTECTED, which includes `«[^»]*»` and `\{%.*?%\}`. Write path: fix_german_connectives.py:170-171 `from store_write import locked_store_rewrite` / `locked_store_rewrite(store, rows, tag='h1302conn')`.
findings.existing_test_gap: german_residue_scan.selftest (german_residue_scan.py:247-267) asserts only that the SCANNER leaves a protected German quote alone (case c, `assert list(scan_text(t3)) == []`); it never calls fix_ru_store. fix_german_connectives.py has no selftest at all, and no module under RussianTranslation/tests/ imports it, so the fixer has never been asserted against a protected span in any test.
findings.fix_boundary: fix_german_connectives.py:121-126 — move MIT_ERGAENZUNG and FEHLERHAFT_FUER out of the full-text block into the `_sub_free_only(..., SCAN_PROTECTED)` call at :128, matching the two spans the detector masks; leave CITATION_ZU / CITATION_BEI / MIT_HEADER on the full text since they key on tag adjacency.

corrections: Three corrections to the finding as written. (1) Severity: P2 -> P3. The failure has never been reachable — across the live store and all 44 historical snapshots, zero phrase-pattern matches ever fell inside a protected span, and the current store has zero matches of either pattern at all; the defect is latent, awaiting a data shape the corpus has never once produced. (2) The failure_scenario's recovery claim is wrong: 'there is no per-row diff to recover it from — only the one-shot .h1302.bak' is refuted by store_write.py:131-134, where locked_store_rewrite unconditionally writes unique_backup_path(store, 'h1302conn') under PromoteClaim before the rewrite, so every run leaves its own timestamped pre-state copy. (3) The existing_test_gap's claim that 'no module ... imports it' and 'fix_german_connectives.py has no selftest at all' is wrong: window_selftest.py:1614 imports fix_ru_store and test_h1302_german_prose_residue_scan already asserts it leaves a protected span untouched — the real, narrower gap is that that assertion exercises only LONE_STORE connectives, never MIT_ERGAENZUNG/FEHLERHAFT_FUER. The fix_boundary at :121-126 is correct and remains worth taking.

findings.title: 93% of the promoted store carries retrospectively backfilled prompt/glossary/script versions with no hashes behind them
findings.invariant: a promoted row identifies the prompt, glossary and script bytes that produced it, so a defect found in any of them has a computable blast radius
findings.failure_scenario: 10,792 of 11,603 rows have pipeline.backfilled=true and carry only prompt_version/glossary_version/script_version = '1.0.0' with prompt_sha, glossary_sha and script_sha ABSENT. Only 811 rows (7.0%) carry the actual content hashes. If a prompt defect is found, the 93% cannot be separated into affected and unaffected -- the version string is an assertion added later, not a measurement.
findings.affected: 10,792 of 11,603 promoted rows
findings.evidence: census over the live store: pipeline keys present on all 11,603 rows are schema/prompt_version/glossary_version/script_version/model_version; prompt_sha/glossary_sha/script_sha present on 811. Independently reached by the contour-3 lane as C3-2 from the code side.
findings.existing_test_gap: no gate refuses a promote whose pipeline block has versions but no shas
findings.fix_boundary: record the shas at promote time and refuse a backfill that invents a version it cannot hash; for the existing 10,792 rows, record the limitation rather than backfilling a second guess

corrections: Two sub-claims are wrong and should be dropped from the write-up. (1) "no gate refuses a promote whose pipeline block has versions but no shas" and the fix "record the shas at promote time" — the live promote path already does: promote_final_cards.py:393 calls pipeline_version.stamp(), which unconditionally computes component_sha for all three components (the H1957 memo removal at pipeline_version.py:118-127 hardened exactly this). A sha-less row is not producible by the promote path; only `pipeline_version.py backfill` makes them. (2) "the 93% cannot be separated into affected and unaffected" is too strong: `backfilled:true` separates asserted-from-measured mechanically, and the min_valid semver mechanism still targets the whole 1.0.0 cohort for re-run at version granularity. The residual, real defect is narrower: the asserted 1.0.0 stamp is unverifiable and cannot be sub-divided within the six generation days, and pwg_ru/REPRODUCIBILITY.md:27-30 presents that stamp as "verified" without the backfill caveat — that doc line, plus a sha-presence counter in audit_translation_provenance.py, is the actual fix boundary. Also worth noting for whoever writes it up: the `script` component set in pipeline_versions.json excludes the harness that actually generated these rows (src/pilot/gen_opt_harness2.py, run_pilot_wf.js), so even the 811 hashed rows hash a set that omits the generator — a separate weakness, not part of L-5.

findings.title: h2189 paid A/B kills the node launcher with the stdlib timeout, orphaning the native Claude child that still holds the API call
findings.invariant: Every kill point that spawns the Windows Claude launcher must terminate the whole process TREE, because `node cli-wrapper.cjs` spawnSync's the native claude binary as a CHILD and `TerminateProcess` on node leaves that binary running and holding the paid API call — the H818 D-J defect `proc_tree.run_tree_kill` exists to close, and which `headless_worker`, `max_account_orchestrator._probe_call`, `profile_status` and `run_claimed` all route through.
findings.failure_scenario: `python src/pilot/h2189_profile_ab.py --run --phase card --arms paid,safe --repeats 2` with the default `--timeout 300.0`. The module's own docstring records card-phase calls at 286 694 ms and 266 349 ms, so the ceiling is reachable. `subprocess.run` raises `TimeoutExpired`, kills only the node process, and returns a row with `failure_class: 'timeout'` and `usage: {}` → `cost_usd_1h_write = 0.0`. The orphaned native binary keeps running against the same `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`; the loop sleeps `--cooldown` (3 s) and starts the NEXT arm's call, so two same-prompt calls are in flight on one profile — the exact cache-accounting confound the docstring says the rig avoids ('Sequential with a cooldown, never parallel: two same-prompt calls in flight at once contaminate each other's cache accounting'). Every create/read number for the following arm is then unattributable, and the A/B verdict rests on it.
findings.evidence: h2189_profile_ab.py:194-201 `proc = subprocess.run(argv, input=stdin, text=True, encoding='utf-8', capture_output=True, timeout=timeout, cwd=cwd, env=env)` … `except subprocess.TimeoutExpired: return {... 'failure_class': 'timeout', 'usage': {}}, None`. The argv is built from the SAME launcher resolver the tree-kill lanes use — h2189_profile_ab.py:78-79 `from headless_worker import (bare_cli_cwd, build_prompt, claude_argv_prefix, parse_cli_wrapper)`, and headless_worker.py:377-380 returns `[node, entries[0]]` on Windows. proc_tree.py:5-10 states the contract this violates verbatim: 'The stdlib timeout kill (TerminateProcess on the immediate node process) leaves that binary ORPHANED, still holding the API call'. The module imports no `proc_tree` symbol (grep of `run_tree_kill|proc_tree` in this file returns nothing). The documented bypasses at h2189_profile_ab.py:54-55 cover the reservation ledger and the profile claim only — not the tree kill.
findings.existing_test_gap: There is no `h2189_profile_ab_selftest.py` and no test in the lane invokes `one_call`; the only offline path is `--check`, which returns before `--run` (line 383-385) and never reaches the spawn. `headless_worker_selftest.py:1979` and `max_account_orchestrator_selftest.py:972` both pin tree-kill behaviour with a real parent/child fixture, but each pins its own module's runner — no test asserts that every claude-spawning site in the tree routes through `proc_tree`, so a new spawn site is invisible to the suite.
findings.fix_boundary: `h2189_profile_ab.one_call` — replace `subprocess.run` with `proc_tree.run_tree_kill(argv, input=stdin, timeout=timeout, cwd=cwd, env=env, capture_output=True)`, which is a documented drop-in and additionally hands back the killed child's drained output for classification.

corrections: Two factual corrections, neither fatal. (1) `existing_test_gap` asserts "There is no `h2189_profile_ab_selftest.py`" — the file exists (src/pilot/h2189_profile_ab_selftest.py, 241 lines, 13 tests). The real gap is narrower and still valid: none of its tests touch `one_call`, the spawn, or tree-kill. (2) The cost half of the failure scenario is REFUTED by that same selftest: `test_failed_call_is_never_priced_at_zero_silently` (line 155) pins that a `failure_class: 'timeout'` row is excluded from `summarise`, and `summarise` (line 269-270) does filter `not r.get('failure_class')` — so the $0 `cost_usd_1h_write` never enters the per-arm medians. Only the ORPHAN half of the harm survives (the still-running native binary contaminating the next same-prefix call's cache accounting), and that is the half that matters. Also: the "286 694 / 266 349 ms" numbers are not in this module's docstring — they are in headless_worker.py:327 and the H2251 ruling doc, and originate from this rig's own H2251 run, which if anything strengthens reachability. Severity is bounded: this is a measurement rig the docstring forbids wiring into a bulk run, so the blast radius is one orphaned paid call plus one invalidated A/B repeat, not production store corruption — P2 is defensible, P3 would not be unreasonable.

findings.title: cloud_window's usage ledger is an unkeyed append — a re-run of the same window double-counts its token/cost telemetry
findings.invariant: Per-call usage telemetry is append-only and must be re-readable idempotently: a re-append of the same call contributes once, exactly as `economy_ledger.dedup_outcomes` dedups on `run_id` (economy_ledger.py:183-209) and `call_reservation` dedups on `reservation_id` (call_reservation.py:227-245) and `emit_call_events` dedups on a stable `call_id` (max_account_orchestrator.py:452-460).
findings.failure_scenario: Lane C drains window `cw_042` (30 items), writes `cw_042.usage.jsonl` with 30 rows, then the routine session dies before the PR is opened. The routine re-runs `run_cloud_window('cw_042', …)` into the same `out_dir`. `wf_output.cw_042.json` is overwritten (30 results), but the ledger is opened `'a'` and gains 30 MORE rows — 60 rows for 30 cards, with no `run_id`, no `call_id`, no reservation id, only `key` and `reserved_at_ns`. Any consumer summing that ledger (the architecture's committed per-lane telemetry, ARCHITECTURE §Key contracts 4) reports ~2x the tokens and ~2x the cost for Lane C, and there is no field in the row that would let a reader collapse the duplicate.
findings.evidence: cloud_window.py:117-120 `ledger = os.path.join(out_dir, '%s.usage.jsonl' % window_id)` / `with open(ledger, 'a', encoding='utf-8', newline='\n') as f: for row in usage_rows: f.write(json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False) + '\n')`. The row shape is fixed at cloud_window.py:86-89 `{'schema': 'pwg.cloud_call.v1', 'key': key, 'reserved_at_ns': t0, 'finalized_at_ns': t1, 'duration_ms': …, 'usage': …}` — no run/call identity. The wf_output beside it is written non-atomically with a plain `open(..., 'w')` at line 115, so a crash mid-write also leaves a truncated result file next to a ledger that already counted its calls. Secondary: line 93 `'selected_keys': [i['key'] for i in items]` includes keys that were PARKED at lines 79-83 and have no entry in `results`, so `selected_keys` over-states the window's scope.
findings.existing_test_gap: `cloud_window.selftest()` (lines 125-175) calls `run_cloud_window` exactly once per `out_dir` and asserts `all(r['finalized_at_ns'] > r['reserved_at_ns'] for r in lrows)` (line 163) — it never calls the same `window_id` twice against the same directory, so the append semantics are never exercised. Assertion (6) at lines 165-172 uses a fresh window with no `out_dir` at all.
findings.fix_boundary: `cloud_window.run_cloud_window` — give each usage row a stable identity (`window_id` + item ordinal, or the `custom_id` shape `pwg_batch._custom_id` already uses) and either dedup on it when appending or write the ledger atomically per window; and stamp `selected_keys` from `results`/`parked` explicitly rather than from `items`.

corrections: Three specific corrections. (a) "no field in the row that would let a reader collapse the duplicate" is false: the ledger is per-window and carries `key`, which is unique per item per run (no retry loop emits a second row for the same key), so `key` is a sufficient collapse key — this is the substantive difference from economy_ledger/call_reservation, where the dedup key is synthetic precisely because the payload has none. (b) The crash-ordering claim is inverted: wf_output is written FIRST (line 115) and the ledger SECOND (118-120), so a crash mid-wf-write leaves a truncated result file with NO ledger rows counted, not "a ledger that already counted its calls". (c) The secondary `selected_keys` claim is wrong by design: elsewhere in the pipeline `meta.selected_keys` denotes the window's requested SCOPE, not its successes — autosplit_requeue.py:708 calls it "the original cards this merge covers — audits reconstruct scope from" it, and coordinator.py:1394-1437 diffs selected_keys against results to derive pending/parked. Including parked keys is required for that diff; stamping it from `results` would break scope reconstruction. What survives is a latent Wave-2 hardening note (make the append idempotent, or write the ledger with 'w' per window) to be handled when Lane C is actually wired, not a live defect at this commit.

findings.title: A freshly created promote claim is momentarily empty, and an empty claim file is judged stale — two promoters can hold the store claim at once
findings.invariant: The claim file's existence must mean 'held' from the instant of creation; the O_EXCL create and the payload write must be one atomic step, because the staleness rule treats an unparseable claim as reclaimable (promote_lock.py:80 `return True  # unreadable/corrupt claim file -> treat as stale`).
findings.failure_scenario: Promoter A executes `os.open(path, O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_WRONLY)` at :140 and is descheduled before `json.dump` at :153 — the claim file exists with zero bytes. Promoter B's O_EXCL fails, `_read()` (:70-75) hits JSONDecodeError and returns None, `claimed_at` is None, `_ts_stale(None)` returns True (:78-80), so `_reclaim(None)` runs: it `os.replace`s A's live claim aside (:99), reads it as empty -> `moved = {}` -> `moved_at = None`, and the restore guard `moved_at != judged_claimed_at` evaluates `None != None` -> False (:110), so it does NOT restore — it deletes the claim (:119) and returns True. B retries O_EXCL and succeeds. A and B now both believe they hold the store claim, and A's `__exit__` (:157-162) will `os.remove` B's claim file. Both then run the read-merge-write window concurrently — the exact last-writer-wins loss this module exists to prevent (promote_lock.py:5-10).
findings.affected: the canonical store under two concurrent promote/mutator runs; also store_write.locked_store_rewrite and every mutator retrofitted onto it
findings.evidence: promote_lock.py:140 `fd = os.open(self.path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_WRONLY)` followed at :152-153 by `with os.fdopen(fd, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:` / `json.dump(self._payload(), f)` — the file is observable, and zero-length, between those statements. promote_lock.py:80 `return True                 # unreadable/corrupt claim file -> treat as stale`. promote_lock.py:110 `if moved_at != judged_claimed_at and not self._ts_stale(moved_at):` — the identity check that is supposed to restore a contender's fresh claim compares None to None and passes through to the delete at :119.
findings.existing_test_gap: promote_lock.selftest (promote_lock.py:166-234) is entirely sequential: every scenario writes a COMPLETE claim file with `json.dump` before testing (:190, :200, :220, :229). The H1386 D2 reclaim test at :217-225 plants a fully-formed contender claim, so the empty-file case — the only one where `judged_claimed_at` and `moved_at` are both None — is never exercised.
findings.fix_boundary: Write the payload with a single `os.write(fd, ...)` before any other process can observe the file, or create the claim as a temp file + `os.replace`; and make `_reclaim` refuse to reclaim when `judged_claimed_at` is None (treat an unparseable claim as busy, requiring --steal-lock).

corrections: The failure_scenario's step "Promoter B's ... `_reclaim(None)` runs: it os.replaces A's live claim aside (:99)" does not hold on the production platform: with A's fd still open, os.replace raises PermissionError (WinError 32), is caught at :100-101 `except OSError: return False`, and B raises ClaimBusy instead of acquiring. Two promoters therefore never both hold the claim on Windows; the observable symptom there is a spurious ClaimBusy, not last-writer-wins loss. The P2 rating assumes a POSIX rename-over-open-file, which no live entry point uses (CI is ubuntu but sequential selftest-only). The logic hole at :110 (`None != None` -> no restore) is real and reproducible in isolation, so the fix_boundary (refuse to reclaim when judged_claimed_at is None; write the payload with a single os.write before the file is observable) is still the right fix — as hardening against a future POSIX/shared-FS deployment, at P3.

findings.title: Retrieval eval leaks the reference translation into the with-TM arm: the hold-out exclusion is applied to the sample TM but not to the publication TM
findings.invariant: A measurement that reports the quality/edit-distance benefit of TM retrieval must retrieve from an index that does not contain the eval card's own reference target; `freeze_batch` is documented as a 'Deterministic stratified hold-out' (tm_retrieval_eval.py:190).
findings.failure_scenario: `tm_retrieval_eval.py run --engine deepseek` freezes cards out of sample400.jsonl (each carrying `target_reference`, tm_retrieval_eval.py:216). At :754 `exclude` is the set of card fragment_ids and is passed only to `sample_tm_rows`. `publication_tm_rows(a.publication)` at :755 is unfiltered, and it mints its own ids of the form `'%s:%d' % (rid, i)` (:288), which can never match a card's fragment_id even if the set were passed. Because sample400 fragments are derived from that same publication TM, an eval card's `source_string` appears verbatim in the index; `retrieve_labse` then classifies it `retrieve_kind='exact'` with `retrieve_score=1.0` and ranks it FIRST (:331-333), and `filter_context` explicitly lets exact hits through for every non-'sense' class (pwg_tm_wave2_policy.py:109). The with-TM arm is handed the gold answer, so `mean_quality`, `mean_edit` and `serious_error_rate` overstate the retrieval benefit by an unknown amount, and `exact_reuse_n` (:428-430) is counted as a feature rather than as leakage.
findings.affected: the RETRIEVAL_EVAL.md / RETRIEVAL_EVAL_LIVE.json quality and edit-distance deltas used to justify wiring retrieval into the wave-2 decode loop
findings.evidence: tm_retrieval_eval.py:754-755 `exclude = {c.get('fragment_id') for c in cards}` / `tm_rows = sample_tm_rows(a.sample, exclude) + publication_tm_rows(a.publication)`. `sample_tm_rows` filters (:305-307 `if fid in exclude_ids: continue`); `publication_tm_rows` (:281-296) takes no exclusion argument at all and assigns synthetic ids at :288. `retrieve_labse` :327-330 `if (row.get('source_string') or '') == src: exact.append(dict(row, retrieve_score=1.0, retrieve_kind='exact'))`, ranked ahead of everything at :353/:377 `ordered = exact + same + other`. A second, smaller hole in the same loop: `run_arm` :422-425 wraps the wave-2 policy filter in `try: ... except Exception: pass`, so if `pwg_tm_wave2_policy` fails to import, the unfiltered context (including 'sense'-class context the policy sets to 'off') is used silently.
findings.existing_test_gap: `selftest` (tm_retrieval_eval.py:821) drives `run_arm` with `_mock_translate_*`/`_mock_judge` and a hand-built tiny index; it never calls `cmd_run`, so the `exclude`/`publication_tm_rows` composition at :754-755 is never executed, and no assertion checks that a card's own `target_reference` is absent from the index it is retrieved against.
findings.fix_boundary: Exclude by normalized `source_string` (and by parent record) rather than by fragment_id, and apply the exclusion to `publication_tm_rows` as well as `sample_tm_rows`; record the leak-check counts in the report meta. Replace the bare `except Exception: pass` at :424-425 with a hard failure so the measured policy is the declared policy.

corrections: Two corrections. (a) MECHANISM: the realized leak does NOT come from the unfiltered `publication_tm_rows` — all three leaking hits carry `origin='promoted'`, i.e. they come from `sample_tm_rows`, which DID receive the exclude set. The real hole is that the exclusion key is `fragment_id` while sample400 contains duplicate fragments with the same `source_string`/`target_string` under different fragment_ids, so excluding the card's own id leaves its twin (and, for `personif.`, two twins) in the index. The publication-TM omission is a genuine latent second hole but is not what produced the observed leak in this data; the fix boundary ("exclude by normalized source_string, not fragment_id") is therefore right for the wrong stated reason. (b) SECONDARY CLAIM: the finding implies the bare `except Exception: pass` at :423-425 may have silently dropped the wave-2 policy, citing that 'sense' context (policy mode `off`) still appears. That inference is wrong — the live run is dated 14 Aug 13:52 and pwg_tm_wave2_policy.py's `'sense': 'off'` default landed at 14:18, after the run. The module imports cleanly today, so the bare-except is a latent hazard only, not a realized one; it should not carry severity. Also note the blast radius is bounded: n=9, and `publication_tm_rows` caps at limit=800, so only the head of the 10 MB publication TM is even in the index.

findings.title: gold_agreement's release-mode guard is disarmed by any non-default input path, and two documented commands use one — so a kappa-free or LLM-panel agreement report can latch the G7 roll-up
findings.invariant: The G7 'double review agreement' gate must be satisfied by measured inter-rater agreement (a kappa on a non-trivial number of double-reviewed items), not by the presence of a report file; G10 (immutable edition cut) must not be declared ready-to-cut on that basis.
findings.failure_scenario: double_review_summary() at line 107-117 computes queue_rows and complete (how many second reviews are actually filled) and labels_jsonl_rows. local_gate_blockers() at line 127-128 then ignores every one of them and blocks G7 only on `not double['agreement_report_exists']` — a bare os.path.exists on gold/double_review_agreement.md (line 104). gold_agreement.py can legitimately produce that exact file with zero double-reviewed items: its release guard (gold_agreement.py:116) fires only when os.path.abspath(path) == os.path.abspath(INP) and --fixture is absent, so `python gold_agreement.py somefile.jsonl ../gold --fixture` writes '| double-reviewed items | 0 |' and '| Cohen kappa | n/a |' (lines 118-123) into the default gold/ directory. preflight then reports G7 'report-present' (line 184), edition_summary() at 136-143 sees no upstream blocker, and sets ready_to_cut=True — G10 is announced ready to cut an immutable edition on zero measured agreement. No kappa threshold exists anywhere in the repo (grep for 'kappa' finds thresholds only in judge_ab_score.py:81 and build_grade_gold.py, neither of which feeds this gate).
findings.evidence: preflight_remaining_gates.py:104 `'agreement_report_exists': os.path.exists(DOUBLE_REVIEW_REPORT)`; :111-114 computes `complete` and never uses it; :127-128 `if not double['agreement_report_exists']: blockers.append('G7_double_review_agreement')`; :143 `'ready_to_cut': not upstream_blockers`; gold_agreement.py:116-123 writes the report with kappa 'n/a' whenever release_mode is False.
findings.existing_test_gap: No test asserts that a 0-pair / kappa-n/a agreement report blocks G7; double_review_verify.py checks the queue shape before review but nothing checks the report content after.
findings.fix_boundary: preflight_remaining_gates.local_gate_blockers must gate on double['complete'] >= a minimum and on a parsed kappa floor from the report (or, better, have gold_agreement emit a machine-readable verdict line the way audit_coverage does), not on file existence.

corrections: The finding is right that double['complete'] and double['queue_rows'] are computed at preflight_remaining_gates.py:111-117 and never consulted by local_gate_blockers:127-128, which makes the G7 belt weaker than the G5/G6 belts beside it. That residual is a cosmetic hardening nit (P3 at most, "tighten the roll-up to match the documented 80/80 volume"), not a P1. Every load-bearing claim built on top of it is wrong: G7 is NOT unblocked (the roadmap status is a separate union term that still blocks), G10 is NOT declared ready-to-cut (I measured ready_to_cut = False under the exact fixture scenario), the edition cut is not gated on ready_to_cut at all (make_edition_cut.py never reads it), and the missing kappa floor is the documented contract, not drift — the manual specifies "needs >=1 kappa pair" as the G7 instrument. The fix_boundary as written would tighten a gitignored dashboard while leaving the real instrument untouched.

Two narrowings, both measured:

1. "unblocking the G10 edition cut" is NOT reachable today. `edition_summary():139` unions `gate_blockers` with `roadmap_blockers()`, and the real `roadmap/quality_gates.jsonl` currently carries `status: partial` for G5, G6 and G7. I ran it: `edition_summary(roadmap_blockers(), ..., [])` -> `ready_to_cut = False, blocked_by = [G5, G6, G7]` even with the empty agreement report present. `ready_to_cut = True` additionally requires a human to hand-edit G7's (and G5's, G6's) status to `passing` in that JSONL. The G7 hole alone does not flip G10 — it only removes the one *measured* check that would contradict such a hand-edit.

2. Nothing enforces `ready_to_cut` anyway. `make_edition_cut.py:129-176` has no gate check at all — `load_gate_statuses()` merely stamps the statuses into `release_manifest.json` and the edition is cut unconditionally. So the harm is a false readiness *report*, not an actually-blocked-then-unblocked cut.

3. State note: `gold/double_review_agreement.md` does not currently exist in the real `RussianTranslation/gold/` directory, so G7 is blocking correctly right now. The defect is one documented command away from latching permanently, not currently mis-reporting.

4. Minor: the MD dashboard (`:183-186`) does surface `complete 0/0` in the detail column, so a careful human reader can see the emptiness; the machine-readable status and the JSON `blocked_by` list do not.

findings.lead_adjudication: Correctness REFUTED the causal chain and is right on every point it makes: `preflight_remaining_gates` is a gitignored dashboard (AGENTS.md:198-210), `edition_summary` can only ADD to `roadmap_blockers()`, the roadmap registry still marks G5/G6/G7 'partial', `make_edition_cut.py` never reads a gate status at all, and a probe run shows `ready_to_cut` staying False. The G10 half of the title is therefore struck entirely. But reproduction CONFIRMED a different and better finding that the correctness lens never reached: `gold_agreement.py:86` computes `release_mode` as `not --fixture AND abspath(path) == abspath(INP)`, so ANY non-default input path silently disarms the >=1-kappa-pair guard — and two commands written in the repo's own docstrings do exactly that (`gold_sample_en.py:26`, `saru_gloss_aggregate.py:258`). Running the second against the real `gold/saru_gloss_double_review.jsonl` emits `double-reviewed items | 109 | Cohen kappa | 0.432` into the default `gold/` directory, i.e. one documented flagless command writes the artifact that latches G7 to 'report-present' on an LLM panel's agreement, not two humans'. Ruling: CONFIRMED at P2 on the disarmable guard, which is the real defect; the roll-up's discarded `complete` count is a P3 hygiene residual noted in the body. `gold/double_review_agreement.md` does not exist today, so G7 is blocking correctly right now — this is one command away from latching, not currently mis-reporting.

findings.title: Headline human-gold precision + Wilson 95% CI computed as if an equal-allocation stratified sample were i.i.d.
findings.invariant: A precision figure published as the store's quality, with a binomial confidence interval, must either come from a simple random sample or be re-weighted by stratum population; equal allocation across strata of very different sizes is neither.
findings.failure_scenario: gold_sample.py:57 sets `per = max(1, n // len(cells))` and line 59-60 draws `random.sample(lst, min(per, len(lst)))` from EVERY (period, kind) cell — the same count from a cell of 400 rows and a cell of 4,000,000. gold_agreement.py:94 then calls stats(final, meta, lambda _: True), which pools all cells (line 69-73) and hands good/n straight to wilson() (line 23-30), and line 99 prints '| precision | %.1f%% (95%% CI %.1f-%.1f) |' into gold/human_precision_report.md — the artifact G6 exists to produce. That number is the unweighted mean over strata, not an estimate of store precision, and the Wilson interval assumes i.i.d. Bernoulli draws that the design does not produce. A cell that is 0.1% of the corpus but 1/12 of the sample moves the headline as much as a cell that is 60% of it. The same pooling is repeated per-period and per-kind at lines 104-112 as post-hoc subgroup CIs with no multiplicity correction. Compounding it, item_labels (lines 49-51) resolves a two-reviewer disagreement with Counter.most_common(1), which on a 1-1 tie silently returns the FIRST-inserted label — so every disagreed item is scored as the first reviewer saw it, and needs_adjudication (ingested at gold_ingest.py:43) is never consulted.
findings.evidence: gold_sample.py:57 `per = max(1, n // len(cells))`; :59-60 equal draw per cell; gold_agreement.py:73 `p, lo, hi = wilson(good, n)`; :94 pooled over all strata; :99 the published CI line; :49-51 `counts.most_common(1)[0][0]` as the adjudicated label.
findings.existing_test_gap: gold_agreement's only guard is the --fixture/release_mode branch at line 86; nothing asserts stratum weights are applied or that a tie is routed to adjudication.
findings.fix_boundary: gold_agreement.stats must accept per-stratum population weights (available from the same corpus_strata.json gold_recall_sample.py:35 already loads) and report a weighted estimate with a design-appropriate interval; ties in item_labels must yield an 'unresolved' bucket, not the first reviewer's label.

corrections: The design flaw is real but the object is misidentified. gold_sample.py + gold_agreement.py measure the Sa-to-Ru HARVEST ALIGNMENT lexicon (corpus_lexicon.jsonl), not the DE-to-RU translation store — the repo's own gold/STORE_DE_RU_GOLD_CUT_SAMPLE_FRAME.md section 1 flags that conflation as the specific over-claim it was written to prevent, and the store's own sampler gold_sample_en.py:70 already draws PROPORTIONALLY (want = max(min(3, len(group)), round(n * len(group) / total))), not equally. findings.title: Provenance 'academic rigor index' denominator drops exactly the cards with no provenance
findings.invariant: A completeness metric must count incomplete records in its denominator; a card missing its provenance block is the failure the metric exists to measure.
findings.failure_scenario: The store loop at lines 103-116 reads prov = c.get('provenance') or {}, computes day = _day(prov.get('generated_at')), and at line 106-107 does `if not day: continue` — BEFORE `total_cards += 1` (line 108) and before cards_by_day is incremented (line 110). A store row whose provenance block is absent, or which carries no generated_at, is therefore excluded from the denominator as well as the numerator. rigor_index at line 204 is _pct(prov_cum[i], cards_cum[i]) — the fraction of *timestamped* cards that also have model_version and pipeline (line 114). Cards with the weakest provenance are invisible, so the index is guaranteed to overstate provenance completeness, and it is a headline value (_headline line 231 'rigor_index_pct') and a trend sentence ('Academic-rigor index (cards with full model+pipeline provenance) at %.0f%%', line 299). This is the metric a reader would use to check the known backfilled-provenance problem, and it is structurally incapable of seeing it. total_cards (line 108) is likewise not the store's card count despite being published as 'total_cards' at line 228.
findings.evidence: pilot/evolution_stats.py:105-108 `day = _day(prov.get('generated_at'))` / `if not day: continue` / `total_cards += 1`; :114 `has_prov = bool(prov.get('model_version')) and bool(prov.get('pipeline'))`; :204 `rigor_index = [_pct(prov_cum[i], cards_cum[i]) ...]`.
findings.existing_test_gap: No test feeds a store containing rows with a missing/timestamp-less provenance block and asserts the rigor index falls.
findings.fix_boundary: Count every store row in a `total_cards`/undated bucket and report rigor as full-provenance / all-rows, surfacing an explicit 'undated' count rather than dropping those rows from the day axis.

findings.title: Daily spot-check: an all-errors judge day exits clean and never trips the R4.1 freeze, contradicting its own 'inconclusive is never PASS' contract
findings.invariant: A judge pass that failed to produce a verdict must not be scored as a passing card; the halt rule must be able to distinguish 'no defects found' from 'nothing was actually judged'.
findings.failure_scenario: judge_card (line 208-209) returns {'status': 'judge_error'} on any exception — missing binary, expired credential, 600 s timeout, unparseable stdout. build_report converts a judge verdict into a defect only under `if judge_results[-1]['status'] == 'judged' and sev == 3` (line 227), so judge_error contributes nothing. sev3_count (lines 230, 240) counts defects only, and main() returns 0 unless sev3_count or san_loss_in_store (line 283). pilot/lane_guard.py:60 — the R4.1 authority — reads only report['sev3_count'] and report['san_loss_in_store'] and has no judge_error branch. A day on which the judge errored on 100% of sampled cards, with the deterministic half finding nothing, is therefore reported and consumed as a clean day: the lane is not frozen and the scheduler sees exit 0. The module docstring at line 27-28 states the opposite: 'A failing/unparseable judge is recorded as judge_error and counts as INCONCLUSIVE, never as PASS (missing evidence is not evidence)' — the recording happens, the counting does not.
findings.evidence: pilot/spot_check_daily.py:208-209 `except Exception ... return {'key': key, 'status': 'judge_error', ...}`; :227 `if judge_results[-1]['status'] == 'judged' and sev == 3`; :230/:240 sev3 counts defects only; :283 `return 1 if (report['sev3_count'] or report['san_loss_in_store']) else 0`; pilot/lane_guard.py:60 `if (report.get('sev3_count') or 0) >= SEV3_FREEZE_THRESHOLD`.
findings.existing_test_gap: selftest at line 341-344 asserts all judge results are judge_error in the broken-judge case but never asserts the report is non-clean or that lane_guard would act; lane_guard's own selftest (lines 178-180) only feeds sev3_count/san_loss.
findings.fix_boundary: Add a judge_error/inconclusive count to the report schema, make main() non-zero on it, and give lane_guard.evaluate an explicit inconclusive branch (freeze or refuse to certify the day).

findings.title: Gold item identity is a positional enumerate index, so re-running the sampler re-binds every human label to a different alignment
findings.invariant: A gold item's id must be a stable function of the item it names, so that human labels collected against id X always describe the same alignment.
findings.failure_scenario: gold_sample.py writes `'id': i` from `for i, r in enumerate(sample)` (lines 63-66). i is a position in a list built by per-cell random.sample (line 60) followed by random.shuffle (line 61) over `cells` derived from the current contents of corpus_lexicon.jsonl (lines 49-55). The fixed SEED (line 56) makes this reproducible only while the lexicon and its cell keys are byte-stable; corpus_lexicon.jsonl is the gitignored ~290 MB regenerated artifact (gold_recall_sample.py:16-17 documents that it is regenerated and relocatable). Downstream, gold_ingest.py:38 carries id through and gold_agreement.item_labels (line 46) keys purely on str(r['id']) — slp1 is carried but never used to verify the join. So if the lexicon is rebuilt and gold_sample re-run, the 320 human labels in gold/_human_gold_review.csv silently attach to different alignments and the precision report in C6-03 measures nothing. gold_packet_verify.py:19 is the only place that keys on (id, slp1), and it only checks packet coverage, never the label join.
findings.evidence: gold_sample.py:56-61 seed/sample/shuffle over lexicon-derived cells; :63 `for i, r in enumerate(sample)`; :66 `'id': i`; gold_agreement.py:46 `by_id[str(r['id'])].append(r['human_label'])`; gold_ingest.py:38 passes id through unverified.
findings.existing_test_gap: gold_validate.py:36-46 checks id non-empty and uniqueness but never that id is derivable from the row's content; no test regenerates the sample and asserts label stability.
findings.fix_boundary: Make id a content hash of (work, group, slp1, kind) as gold_sample writes it, and have gold_ingest/gold_agreement verify slp1 agreement on the join before accepting a label.

corrections: The stable-identity requirement is already satisfied by the committed gold/gold_set.jsonl, which is what the reviewer CSV and all label artifacts are keyed to. The finding is right only about a much smaller thing, worth at most P3: gold_review_csv.py:37/51 joins the gitignored gold_sample.jsonl by positional id purely to fill src_sa/src_ru/src_comm, so a lexicon rebuild + gold_sample re-run before a CSV export would show reviewers source verses belonging to a different alignment than the sa/ru they are judging. Fix boundary is one line in load_context/main — verify c.get('slp1') == g.get('slp1') before using the context, and blank it otherwise. No change is needed in gold_ingest.py or gold_agreement.py.

findings.title: det_gate passes a card that emitted ZERO senses, and reports coverage 1.0, when the source has <=1 declared sense and no masked spans
findings.invariant: The shared A/B free gate must reject a card that dropped all its content before the paid Opus controller ever sees it; both arms must be gated identically.
findings.failure_scenario: deterministic_audit computes issues from four checks. The {Tn} multiset checks (lines 78-99) are vacuous when c['skeleton_tokens'] is empty and the card invented no placeholders — true for the many PWG/NWS single-gloss and supplement cards that carry no <ls>/{#…#}/<ab> spans (audit_coverage.py:14-16 documents that whole class as 'not sense-divided'). The sense-shortfall check at line 102 is guarded by `src > 1`, so a source with source_senses of 0 or 1 can never trip it.
